Burnham made similar ­complaints on Wednesday despite ­Everton ­having admitted ­breaching ­profitability and sustainability rules, with the club contesting only the extent of the breach and sanction. “I remember people proclaiming Everton guilty at the time and, with hindsight, I think more people would say that wasn’t fair the way that was handled,” he said. “I still hold the view very firmly that they weren’t fairly treated in that process.”

The Premier League was unhappy with Burnham’s behaviour in 2023, particularly as his office posted on X two letters of complaint he sent to the league, but did not publicise replies sent by Brittain that explained the competition’s financial regulations governance process.

The Independent Football Regulator chief executive, David Kogan, has made clear he will not tolerate political interference in his role, telling the Times last year that he would resign if he sensed ­government pressure.

The City case has the potential to present an early test of his ­mettle and the IFR’s powers, given ­Burnham’s previous working relationship with the club’s owner, the Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG), and the £25bn annual UK-Abu Dhabi ­trading ­relationship. One of Burnham’s first calls after he succeeded Sir Keir Starmer in July was with Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, ­president of the United Arab ­Emirates and the ultimate owner of ADUG.

Kogan confirmed the IFR was monitoring the case and has powers “to assess the suitability of owners, directors and executives” to protect “honesty and integrity of English football where there is clear evidence of wrongdoing by individuals”.

City’s owners are unlikely to fall foul of the licensing system that will be introduced next season, because that is an assessment of financial sustainability and separate from the new owners, directors and senior executives test, which the IFR uses to examine honesty and integrity.

The Premier League and IFR declined to comment.

Sports.title: Neco Williams fires revitalised Wales to fightback win against 10-man Norway
Sports.content:
On a night when Erling Haaland moped around the pitch, dragging his hulking frame across the Cardiff turf, Wales registered a welcome victory over 10-man Norway and their first this year. Was this just one of those games where the game’s deadliest finisher was stuck on the fringes or was it a case of 115 things occupying his mind? Either way, this defeat proved a humbling experience. “You’re just a shit Kieffer Moore,” was the chant aimed at Haaland from the locals.

Daniel James cancelled out Oscar Bobb’s well-worked opener in the first half and 17 seconds after the restart Torbjørn Heggem was sent off for fouling James as the Leeds winger streamed towards goal, resulting in a free-kick from which Neco Williams earned Craig Bellamy a timely win with an unerring strike.

“It feels a bit like the first punch in the face in a long, long time,” said the Norway and Arsenal captain Martin Ødegaard after his country lost successive games for the first time in four years. “Now we have to respond, stick together and fight back.”

For Bellamy, a first win since last November eased the mounting negativity after a bruising run of results, chiefly their World Cup playoff defeat to Bosnia and Herzegovina in March and a listless display in Denmark last Sunday. “I felt my own disappointment since Bosnia and I’ve felt the stick as well,” the Wales head coach said. “The summer wasn’t easy. These games weren’t easy. But I’ve seen it … I’ve seen managers before me get it. I’ve seen the abuse the previous manager [Rob Page] got. It’s been a really difficult couple of months but it’s ‘welcome to this’ if you want to step into this … this is it. I do think we could be kinder to each other.”

It was plain to see Bellamy had been hurting and he cited his daughter receiving abuse on social media. “I chose to live back down here because I wanted to be on the ground, I wanted to be called a wanker to my face,” he added.

View image in fullscreen Torbjørn Heggem sees red straight after half-time. Photograph: Nick Potts/PA

“The World Cup [playoff defeat] moved, I just felt the shift … Look, I am a strong person, I think we all are, but it’s the people around me I’m conscious of. It’s just society. What are we? Eight prime ministers in the space of 11 years? It’s nuts ... We’re such a small country, why can’t we have each other’s backs? Why don’t we look after each other more? The others can go at us. We’re too quick [to criticise].”

View image in fullscreen Dan James brings Wales level in the first half. Photograph: Nick Potts/PA

Wales bounced off the canvas after Ødegaard’s cute ball released Bobb on goal to open the scoring on 11 minutes. Liam Cullen, now of third-tier Leicester, pinched the ball from Sander Berge after the Fulham ­midfielder was sluggish to claim Fredrik Aursnes’s pass and Wales raced away from the scene.

Cullen and Lewis Koumas burst forward and Sorba Thomas zipped a low cross into the box, where James beat David Møller Wolfe to the punch. Thomas, who by his own admission loves staying wide to get chalk on his boots, was a constant threat.

Norway were punished for being slow out of the blocks in the second half, Heggem hauling James down after the restart. James does everything at speed and Heggem knew he was in trouble. The Spanish referee Alejandro Hernández awarded a free-kick on the edge of the box and ­Williams dispatched a wonderful right-foot strike to Ørjan Nyland’s right, to the surprise of the former Aston Villa and Reading goalkeeper.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Bobb played draught excluder behind a white wall of Norway shirts and Nyland stepped to his left. Nyland was out of position when he had to shuttle across his goalline when Williams thrashed the ball into the bottom corner.

Haaland had one of those games; he was on the periphery and recorded just 11 first-half touches, the fewest of any player, including the Borussia Dortmund full-back Julian Ryerson who was forced off through injury after 16 minutes. Ethan Ampadu easily won what, technically, will go down as a duel on halfway but in truth Haaland just stuck out a leg in the hope of claiming the ball. His first whiff of goal came a couple of minutes before the interval but Ryerson’s replacement, Marcus Pedersen, misread Haaland’s movement and the move collapsed.

The substitute Josh Sheehan spurned a golden chance to extend Wales’s advantage, sending a weak shot at Nyland after more fine craftsmanship from Thomas to release the Bolton midfielder on goal. Up the other end, Haaland ambled across the box in preparation for another Pedersen cross. When it arrived Haaland soared high but unmarked sent a header straight at Danny Ward. Then came a puff of the cheeks, a look to the turf. It has been that kind of week.

Sports.title: Nations League: Ronaldo-less Portugal prosper while Klopp gets first win as Germany coach
Sports.content:
Portugal maintained their perfect start to Nations League Group A4 as Jorge Jesus’s squad showed little signs of missing Cristiano Ronaldo with a 4-2 victory over Denmark in Copenhagen.

The 41-year-old Al-Nassr forward and five-time Ballon d’Or winner left the camp before the match amid reports of a falling out with Jesus, his former club manager, having been left on the bench throughout a victory in Norway.

João Cancelo gave Portugal a 13th-minute lead before Brentford midfielder Mikkel Damsgaard equalised.

Gonçalo Ramos swiftly put Portugal back in front after 25 minutes, with Napoli forward Rasmus Højlund levelling things up at 2-2 early in the second half following a swift counter.

Vitinha’s header, his first Portugal goal, and a late strike by João Félix made it three straight wins.

“A victory of the highest quality,” said Jesus. “This Portugal team scored four goals and put in a performance which, in my opinion, was of a very high standard – and that cannot be overlooked. Of course, this is more important than anything else that has happened.”

New Germany head coach Jürgen Klopp got his first win with a 2-0 Group A2 victory over Serbia in Munich. Bayern Munich midfielder Tom Bischof fired in his first senior international goal and Liverpool forward Florian Wirtz then added a second in the 61st minute.

Germany produced a disciplined and intensive game, illustrating the high-pressure soccer Klopp wants to instill in the team. “That’s going in my archive. We’ll make a video out of it now,” Klopp said. “That’s how we want to play.”

View image in fullscreen Jürgen Klopp (right) applauds fans alongside Tom Bischof, who scored his first international goal in the victory over Serbia. Photograph: Angelika Warmuth/Reuters

Speaking to public broadcaster ZDF, he added: “The mix of football and attitude was top level today. I told the boys that this has to be our benchmark.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Wirtz said: “It was important to win again, just for the spirit in the team, and to send a signal out that we’re good football players and also a good football nation. Definitely a step in the right direction.”

In the same group, Tijjani Reijnders scored a late equaliser as the Netherlands fought back to draw 2-2 with Greece, who remain top. Fotis Ioannidis and Giorgos Masouras had the home side 2-0 up at the break.

Liverpool defender Virgil van Dijk powered in a header from a corner on the hour. After Denzel Dumfries had seen his goal ruled out by VAR for offside, Reijnders lashed home a rebound in the 89th minute to secure a point.

In Group B3, Israel and Kosovo played out a goalless draw in Debrecen, Hungary. In Group D1, Malta and Gibraltar drew 1-1 while in Group D2, Azerbaijan were held to a goalless draw by Liechtenstein in Baku.

Sports.title: Shaw secures WCL draw against Real Madrid as Manchester City show spirit after week of turmoil
Sports.content:
Andrée Jeglertz, the Manchester City head coach, said the noise surrounding the guilty verdict dished out by the Premier League had zero impact on his women’s team’s performance after they played out a high-quality draw with Real Madrid in the Women’s Champions League.

Khadija ‘Bunny’ Shaw’s ruthless finish earned City a point against an impressive Real Madrid side on a night when the hosts were surely glad for attentions to turn – however briefly – towards on-pitch matters after a week when the wider football club has dominated the headlines for the wrong reasons.

“Of course there is a lot of noise but the players are very calm – I haven’t seen or noticed anything that will take any percentage out of the players’ performance,” Jeglertz said.

The result – which was a fair reflection of an even but entertaining game – left both sides with two points from their opening two fixtures but City will know their league phase opponents should theoretically become less challenging from hereon after their opening draw at Bayern Munich. The Swedish coach added: “It is OK, it’s an OK start in the Champions League. It’s not ideal but it’s a good start and we know what is needed from us in the rest of the tournament.”

Quick Guide WCL roundup: PSG pummel Leuven Show The day after Paris FC played their first Women’s Champions League home game at Stade Jean-Bouin, across the road from Paris Saint-Germain’s Parc des Princes, PSG’s women’s team entertained Leuven 20km away at the club’s suburban training centre. Rasheedat Ajibade put the hosts ahead from close range after nine minutes against the Belgian side. Naomie Feller (pictured) then scored a quick-fire double, before Sakina Karchaoui and Vitória Yaya completed PSG's 5-0 rout. In the early games, Modesta Uka scored Austria Vienna’s first goal in the WCL but Inter's captain, Ivana Andrés, levelled in the fourth minute of added time to earn a 1-1 draw. Inter dropping points left Barcelona, who thrashed Roma on Wednesday, as the only WCL team with six points after two games. In a match between two teams that had lost in the opening round, HB Køge crushed visiting Swiss team Servette 5-1 in Denmark. PA Photograph: Benoît Tessier/REUTERS Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Jeglertz had been at pains to insist that it has been “business as usual” for his team despite the damning guilty verdict released by the Premier League towards the men’s side. There was a strange mood around this stadium in the buildup to kick-off with opinions mixed.

Speaking to supporters on the bridge that connects this venue with the neighbouring Etihad Stadium, some appeared relaxed about the situation and unsure what it had to do with the women’s team, while others were clearly troubled and looking forward to watching some football as a form of escapism.

View image in fullscreen Khadija Shaw fires home Manchester City’s equaliser early in the second half. Photograph: Martin Rickett/PA

An elderly City fan, who did not wish to be named, said pre-match: “We’ve been through rough times before, we’ll come through rough times again,” in a matter-of-fact manner. Another simply demonstrated what appears to be a growing dislike for reporters asking about the 115 charges when they said angrily “you’re from the media?” before using an expletive and promptly walking away.

A much politer, younger woman simply expressed her sadness and her hopes that it wouldn’t cause the players stress.

Once the match started, there were occasional references to the news from the stands; midway through the first half one home fan sang ‘Sheikh Mansour, my lord, Sheikh Mansour, oh lord, Sheikh Mansour’, to the tune of Kumbaya, although nobody else appeared to join in. There was also a small group of men carrying an inflatable banana in one corner defiantly chanting about ‘City going down with a billion in the bank’.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

In general, though, the regular Women’s Super League match-going fans who are members of the supporters club seemed focused on their usual repertoire of fan chants to encourage the players, whether singing about the brilliance of Aoba Fujino and later chanting the name of Mary Fowler, who hit the crossbar with a header before the break.

By then Real Madrid were already ahead courtesy of Linda Caicedo’s clinical, low finish into the bottom corner after a lethal burst of pace. The visitors could have scored as early as the first minute, when a sloppy mistake by Carlotta Wamser allowed Felicia Schröder to shoot but her effort flew narrowly wide and bounced off the stanchion, rippling the net but from the wrong side. It was a sign of the Spanish team’s intent and they looked sharp throughout.

City’s play was significantly more urgent and incisive after the break and – after Yui Hasegawa spurned a volleyed chance when she was in space inside the box – it did not take long for the hosts to equalise. Shaw turned and clinically fired into the corner of the net with great technique after good pressing from City led to Hasegawa winning the ball in midfield and feeding Shaw in the area. It was the Jamaica striker’s fifth goal of the season in all competitions and her first of this Champions League campaign.

Suddenly the WSL champions were dominating the territory, although Caicedo did go close at the other end with a diagonal shot that bounced wide. The introductions of Beth Mead, Sam Coffey and Grace Clinton from City’s bench only seemed to further strengthen the hosts.

Hasegawa volleyed just wide again, this time from the second phase after a half-clear corner, in another let-off for Real Madrid, who had gone close themselves at the other end when Ayaka Yamashita did well to save from Caicedo. The home fans were on their feet to applaud Yamashita and chant her name when she later produced a quick reaction save to keep out Irune Dorado’s close-range effort and keep the score level.

Sports.title: Pro-Palestine protests interrupt game as Ireland pass up 2-0 lead in draw against Austria
Sports.content:
Protests halted events in Dublin twice before the Republic of Ireland were forced to settle for a 2-2 draw after Austria came back in the second half of their Nations League encounter at the Aviva Stadium.

Despite a significant security presence, the contest was twice interrupted in the opening 45 minutes, first due to what campaign group Stop the Game later referred to in a statement as a “limited tennis ball protest”, when – around the 20th minute – tennis balls wrapped in stickers featuring the Palestinian flag and the text “#StopTheGame” were launched on the pitch.

Then around the 35th minute a man ran on to the field of play from the opposite side carrying what appeared to be a Palestinian flag and was immediately tackled by security and carried off.

It has been a tumultuous week for the Republic. Their two Nations League fixtures against Israel have divided opinion in the country, sparking protests, including one which took place pre-match outside the stadium. The Republic’s behind-closed-doors “home” game against Israel in Backa Topola, Serbia, is scheduled for Sunday, and the manager Heimir Hallgrímsson on Wednesday confirmed it was their intention to play.

Troy Parrott got the hosts under way with a sensational 12th-minute opener and added a penalty on the stroke of half-time.

A pair of substitutes proved the Republic’s undoing after Alexander Prass halved the deficit in the 71st minute and Michael Gregoritsch drew the sides level six minutes later.

View image in fullscreen Michael Gregoritsch (left) points to the sky after scoring Austria’s second goal. Photograph: Brian Lawless/PA

Hallgrímsson’s men had a chance to top Group B3 with a victory, but they sit third behind Austria and Kosovo at the halfway point of the group stage.

Hallgrímsson made three changes, including the re-introduction of Finn Azaz, who was greeted warmly when his name was announced over the PA system before the match.

The goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu, who had made himself unavailable for the Israel meetings, was back in the squad, while Liam Scales and John Egan were awarded starts.

There was an audacious early effort from Sasa Kalajdzic, who tried to catch Caoimhín Kelleher off his line with a lob from midfield, before the Republic enjoyed a couple of attacking spells deep in the visitors’ half.

It was a brilliant opener from Parrott, who realised he was on his own after bringing down Adam Idah’s glanced-on header from a goal kick.

View image in fullscreen Troy Parrott slots home the Republic of Ireland’s opening goal in the 12th minute. Photograph: Evan Treacy/EPA

The Real Betis striker was sandwiched in a triangle of white shirts before nutmegging Philipp Lienhart and evading every other challenger with a mazy run before planting the ball past Florian Wiegele and into the bottom corner.

Play was briefly paused just before the 20th minute to clear up the tennis balls, a pause both teams used for a hydration break. The second stoppage of play took place around the 35th minute.

Kelleher denied Patrick Wimmer and there were a few more promising spells for Austria before Parrott doubled their lead. Ryan Manning won the penalty after he was clipped in the box by Nicolas Seiwald. Parrott stepped up after a video assistant referee check and blasted it past the Austria keeper.

Austria cut the deficit after Liam Kitching was caught out and Austria worked the ball to the unmarked Prass, who blasted the ball beyond Kelleher. The offside flag was initially raised, but the decision was reversed by VAR.

The Brentford keeper then failed to stop Gregoritsch, guessing the wrong way as the Augsburg forward fired into the corner.

The Republic captain, Dara O’Shea, was denied by an excellent leaping Wiegele save, Gregoritsch directed a shot over the crossbar, and both sides fended off attempts at a late winner.

Sports.title: Jürgen Klopp disgusted by claims his Germany team are ‘not white enough’
Sports.content:
Jürgen Klopp has reacted with disgust to a social media debate questioning whether the Germany team he is in the process of forming are “white enough”. Klopp said he believed there was no point in giving room to “such people and their utterances”, dismissing them as “complete nonsense”.

Asked to respond to the debate as to whether the national team were “not German enough” or “not white enough”, he said: “There is absolutely no reason to pay attention to these people. You won’t get my thoughts on this. I have little time in everyday life for idiocy – and even less on social media.

“The great crux of our lives is that everyone is allowed to express their opinion … it’s insane when something like that exists.”

Klopp said watching sportspeople interact with each other was proof to him that mutual respect was still possible. “The world could learn a thing or two from a sports changing room … There, everyone is respected based on the facts and not discredited based on false opinions.”

Klopp, whose plans for Germany since he took over as coach in the summer have attracted huge attention, said the players he had gathered at the national team camp, including several players with a migrant background, “could not be better united than they are”.

The barrage of racist and generally offensive commentaries on social media followed Germany’s 1-0 defeat by Greece last Sunday, in the Nations League, marking the first time Greece had beaten Germany.

It is also reflective of plenty of utterances from MPs of the far-right Alternative für Deutschland (AfD), the largest opposition party in the Bundestag, who have repeatedly and consistently criticised the diversity and ethnic makeup of the national team, often referring to the squad in derogatory terms such as a “politically correct mercenary force”.

Klopp, who has a four-year contract running until the end of the 2030 World Cup, was speaking before Germany’s Nations League match on Thursday against Serbia.

Sports.title: US lined up instead of Qatar to host inaugural Women’s Club World Cup
Sports.content:
The US is poised to host the first Women’s Club World Cup in January 2028, becoming the latest in a series of major Fifa tournaments staged in North America. Discussions to take the competition to the US are at an advanced stage, with Los Angeles and San Diego among the favoured host cities.

It will follow the men’s tournament, whose expanded version debuted last year, in being staged by a country that also hosted the men’s World Cup this summer.

While a deal is yet to be confirmed, the path has cleared for the US to hold the 19-team event without going through a formal bidding process, even though Qatar was in talks with Fifa about hosting.

The winter scheduling will avoid a clash with the men’s Copa América, which the US is the frontrunner to host in June and July 2028, but raises the prospect of a hectic year-round calendar for the world’s top players. The Club World Cup is placed squarely between the 2027 Women’s World Cup and the 2028 Olympics, which will demand full-strength squads. A number of top clubs are in favour of a rule change limiting players to one international tournament per year, whether for club or country.

Fifa is keen to use the Club World Cup as a dry run for the 2031 Women’s World Cup, which the US will host in conjunction with Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica in a decision to be formally approved at an Extraordinary Fifa Congress on 23 November.

Football’s global body is eager to assess the stadium venues, pricing and demand for tickets at the smaller 19-team Club World Cup before the 48-team World Cup three years later. Time to organise and market the Club World Cup is tight, given it will start on 5 January 2028.

Sources have cited the chaos engulfing Fifa’s leadership since the emergence of Gianni Infantino’s ill-fated FFE scheme as a significant reason for the backlog of hosting decisions still to be taken. In July, Europe’s top clubs threatened not to participate in future Club World Cups unless the FFE project was shelved. They also warned the threat would hold unless a joint venture between European Football Clubs and Fifa, agreed in outline form, but yet to be signed off, was completed before television rights could be sold for the women’s Club World Cup.

Another tournament awaiting a venue is the 2029 men’s Club World Cup. The US has expressed interest in hosting that competition, but should the women’s event be confirmed it appears more likely to be co-hosted by Morocco, Spain and Portugal before they jointly host the men’s World Cup the following year.

Sports.title: Yemen and football in the face of civil war: ‘It would be very nice to give the world a different headline’
Sports.content:
The Yemen national coach, Noureddine Ould Ali, chose not to reach for a good old-fashioned football excuse after his team’s 1-0 loss to Qatar in the Gulf Cup on Saturday, despite a clear penalty not given their way. The defeat meant the Reds crashed out of the eight-team regional tournament, taking place in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, with a game of the group stage remaining.

There are other factors the Algerian could list for a defeat against a team that was at the World Cup. Qatar have the Aspire Academy, state of the art stadiums and a former Spain and Real Madrid coach – Julen Lopetegui – in charge. Yemen have nothing approaching that and have not played a home game since 2012, a 2-1 win over Palestine in Sanaa.

Two years later, the capital city came under the control of the Houthis, an Iran-backed militant group, provoking a Saudi-led intervention and years of fighting. The United Nations brokered a truce in 2022 that did reduce hostilities, but the situation has escalated again. In early September, the Houthis swept down the Red Sea coast in its first major military advance in five years and have been targeting Riyadh and other places in Saudi Arabia with missile strikes.

View image in fullscreen Yemen will play in the Asian Cup in January for the second time, managing to qualify despite political turmoil in their country. Photograph: Sipa US/Alamy Live News

At the time, the national team had been training in the southern port city of Aden, home of the presidential leadership council, Yemen’s internationally recognised, Saudi-backed, governing body. “The situation in Aden was OK. We tried our best and had a training camp with local players and then we joined up with the rest of the squad in Jeddah,” Ould Ali says.

“The situation is a political situation and it is not stable. In football we have to be careful. We have a lot of attention on outside factors, but we always try to focus on the football and do better. In Saudi Arabia, the welcome has been great, the people are very friendly and there is a high level of training facilities, hotels and everything. It means we could focus on football.”

Losing 4-0 to the United Arab Emirates in the opener was a reality check, but the UAE have a lot of naturalised talent from overseas to count on and even Andrés Iniesta coaching in the domestic second tier. Yemen barely has a top tier with the local league affected by the fighting. They still beat Bahrain 5-2 in their final group game.

“The league stopped for a long time and restarted this year and they finished the first half of the season,” Ould Ali says. “It is very important. The players need to play, need to keep fit and show their talent.

“The people support us. It is a religion in Yemen. Everyone likes football and the national team and follows their star players. The Yemeni people are the same as anyone else.”

Most of the players are based at home and before the 27th edition of the Gulf Cup, Yemen was the only one of the eight never to have won the tournament and have never got out of the group.

It is hard for the players to keep fully focused on football while in Saudi Arabia. “They worry about what is going on in the country and they hope their families are OK,” the coach said. “This is normal, but they are professional and I ask them to try to focus on the games. I have lived this situation before, I have geopolitics experience in the region.”

Ould Ali spent three years in charge of Palestine from 2018 to 2021, after more than four years as an assistant coach. Instability is not an unfamiliar theme for him. “Each situation is different. Yemen is a problem between Yemenis, not between outside countries.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Fortnightly Sign up to The Hotspot A new fortnightly newsletter covering the intersection of sport and the climate crisis Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Algeria’s Noureddine Ould Ali is used to instability. He coached Palestine before his stint with Yemen. Photograph: ZUMA Press Inc/Alamy Live News

“For a coach, Palestine was very difficult. The Israeli soldiers used to stop me for eight to 10 hours before I could go to work. The players are not free and when we played overseas they stopped the players. It was a pleasure for me to work with Palestine, their difficulties are not made by Palestinians.”

A reunion with Palestine is not impossible at the 2027 Asian Cup, which will also be hosted in Saudi Arabia. In June, Yemen, slightly surprisingly, defeated Lebanon to become the last team to qualify for the quadrennial tournament. “It was a great day for Yemen football and we hope we could make people back home smile for a while.”

In January, Yemen return to Jeddah for their opening game against South Korea and players such as Atlético Madrid’s Lee Kang-in, Kim Min-jae of Bayern Munich and Son Heung-min. It will be a step up from the Gulf Cup and the people back home will be watching.

“Again, we will try to make the people at home proud,” says Ould Ali. “It would be very nice to give the world a different headline about Yemen. When we are united we feel we can beat anyone.”

Sports.title: Jorge Jesus insists he has a 'clear conscience' and team remains united despite Cristiano Ronaldo saga amid rift with captain - as Portugal beat Denmark in first match since star's sensational walk-out
Sports.content:
Portugal manager Jorge Jesus is standing firm amid a rift with Cristiano Ronaldo that saw the superstar forward leave the national team camp.

Ronaldo, 41, landed in Madrid in the early hours of Thursday morning after flying from Copenhagen, where Portugal faced Denmark on Thursday, on his private jet. He had been seen leaving the Parken Stadium in the Danish capital on Wednesday after missing a third consecutive training session.

Ronaldo later confirmed in a statement on Instagram that he had left the team's camp because of comments made by Jesus in his press conference.

The Portugal boss said the captain would not start the Denmark clash, just days after sitting on the bench for the entirety of the 2-1 win in Norway, but insisted there was no issue between the two.

Jesus, meanwhile, who took over from Roberto Martinez after the World Cup, oversaw a 4-2 win for his side on Thursday night, and insisted he remains in control of the team – with full faith from the players.

'I don't have a group in my hand. I have a group that believes in the coach's ideas,' he said. 'They believe in my ideas and, because they have a lot of individual quality, things become easier.

'If that's having a group in my hand, then I do, because they go hand in hand with me and my ideas.'

Portugal manager Jorge Jesus insists he is in control of his players and has a 'clear conscience' amid his feud with Cristiano Ronaldo

Ronaldo left the Portugal camp after taking issues with words in his manager's press conference before they faced Denmark

Reports in Portugal claim Ronaldo could be suspended from playing for his country for between one and six months if he is found to have 'abandoned' the team.

The Portuguese Football Federation's disciplinary code states: 'Any player who, having been regularly called up, unjustifiably abandons or fails to appear for training, a match, or any activity of the national teams or related to the sporting representation of the FPF or Portugal, will be sanctioned with a suspension of one to six months.'

Ronaldo said: 'After the national team coach's press conference, and following a conversation with the President of the Portuguese Football Federation, I have decided to leave the national team training camp.

'In due time, I will tell all Portuguese people the truth about the reasons that led to my departure from the national team, to which I have always dedicated myself.

'Now is the time to wish good luck to Portugal and to all my teammates.'

Jesus, though, who also managed Ronaldo at Al-Nassr insists his conscience is clean.

'It's not difficult for me to focus,' he added. 'You know what's difficult for me? It's not understanding what's going on inside. It's not knowing how to train my players. That's what's difficult for me. The rest... zero.

'What's important is what we have to do. The things that happen don't separate the group, they haven't separated us and they won't separate us.'

One group of fans showed support for Jesus in the stands as Portugal beat the Danes 4-2

The support, however, was split, with some making it clear they were siding with Ronaldo

Jesus received support in the stands from some of Portugal's fans, with one fan group each wearing a shirt spelling out: 'Love u Jesus'. Other fans held up banners with Ronaldo's face and name on.

Speaking before the Denmark game, Jesus insisted he had a 'completely' clear conscience amid the Ronaldo saga. 'It was a frantic few hours because we had two games,' he added.

'Now we have another one... Besides, I've been in football for many years and I know I didn't do anything to prevent the situation from continuing as before.'

Footage published by A Bola showed Jesus and Proenca being booed by a small group of fans who had gathered outside the team's hotel in Copenhagen before the team made the short journey to Parken Stadium.

Ronaldo held talks with Jesus and Proenca on Wednesday morning, a meeting initially described as amicable. But the rift between Ronaldo and his manager appeared to deepen after Jesus's press conference.

Jesus admitted Ronaldo had been 'angry' with him, with footage showing the captain walking off down the tunnel after sitting out the victory in Norway.

Jesus said: 'There was no incident whatsoever. Any player - and I was a player myself - when you spend 20 or 30 minutes warming up and then don't get on, no-one is happy about that.

'Afterwards, as coach, I decided not to bring him on. It's nothing to make a fuss about.'

Jesus also suggested Goncalo Ramos would keep his place in the side ahead of Ronaldo for the Denmark match. 'If I need (Ronaldo), he'll come on,' he said. 'If I don't need him, he won't.'

Jesus had originally planned to bring on the veteran striker for a 30-minute cameo but then decided to leave him on the bench, which has seemingly sparked the feud.

Sports.title: Ireland's clash with Austria is HALTED as furious fans throw hundreds of tennis balls onto the pitch in protest at matches against Israel going ahead
Sports.content:
Ireland's clash with Austria is HALTED as furious fans throw hundreds of tennis balls onto the pitch in protest at matches against Israel going ahead

Ireland saw their Nations League game against Austria brought to a halt as fans protested their matches against Israel.

There was doubt over the weekend whether Ireland would fulfil their fixtures against Israel this international break, but the first game was played at the weekend and the second is scheduled to take place too.

Ireland beat Israel 3-0 in their first fixture in Hungary on Sunday night, with goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu having pulled out of the highly-charged match on ethical grounds. A petition to stop the game going ahead had been signed by almost 20,000.

Hundreds of pubs in Ireland refused to show the first encounter and have vowed to do so again for Sunday's game, while there were protests outside the team hotel in Dublin.

The players did not shake hands, and Israel's captain and FA spoke out against the team after the match.

On Thursday, meanwhile, fans launched tennis balls onto the field at the 20-minute mark at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin to protest the games taking place. Some balls were wrapped in stickers featuring the Palestinian flag and the text #StopTheGame.

Ireland's game against Austria was paused after fans threw tennis balls onto the pitch at the Aviva Stadium

A fan with a Palestine flag also ran onto the field with several members of security ejecting him

One fan, roughly 15 minutes later, also ran onto the field waving a Palestine flag, with a number of security personnel required to remove them.

A majority of players, meanwhile, described as 'significant' by the Football Association of Ireland, ultimately elected to fulfil their 'away' clash on Sunday.

A 'Stop The Game' campaign – organised by the pressure group Irish Sport for Palestine called for fans to gather ahead of the match with Austria to voice opposition to Sunday's match with Israel.

Ireland captain Dara O'Shea did not shake hands with Israel's skipper Manor Solomon at the coin toss last week, and Ireland wore black armbands 'in recognition of all lives lost in the (Gaza) conflict'.

The Ireland players also snubbed the Israeli National Anthem by pointedly looking at the ground while it played.

The second match against Israel will take place behind closed doors in Serbia.

Bazunu was the only member of the squad to officially make himself unavailable for selection for the Israel matches, but the Bolton goalkeeper chose to remain with the team and be with them for the Austria match.

He will then be replaced in the squad by Josh Keeley for the second fixture with Israel.

Some balls appeared to have Palestine stickers on - Ireland will take on Israel for a second time in eight days on Sunday

Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson had previously said his team are 'playing against genocide' amid Israel's attacks on Palestine, where more than 70,000 people have been killed since the war in Gaza began, according to the territory's Hamas-run health ministry.

He also criticised 'lies' that had been reported concerning Bazunu's withdrawal from the first fixture and insisted there is a 'strong bond' in his squad.

'Gavin is a great lad. I've always had a good relationship with him and it's probably more tough for him than the other players, but they have really welcomed him,' said Hallgrimsson. 'There's been a lot of lies said around all of this, but we welcome him back and he's taken part, amazing.

'I think it shows his character, as well, to be with us, so I want to give him praise for that. I want to give the players praise for how welcome they have been with him.

After Sunday's game, Israel captain and west Ham winger Manor Solomon hit out at his Irish opponents, saying: 'They said nonsense during the game, I don't want to talk about them.

'If I say what I think about them, I'll probably be banned for a few games so I don't want to say. Of course they hate us and we don't like them.

'I'm already looking forward to the next game against them, it's going to be completely different. What they did with the anthem? I'm not interested in them, we have a country that is ten times better than theirs, stronger, an amazing country with amazing people. (They) can play all their tricks. We are Israelis and love the country. And that will always be the case.'

The episode is the latest sign of growing hostility towards Israel and comes weeks after 12 countries including the UK, France and Canada announced sanctions on illegal Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank.

Goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu withdrew from the squad to face Israel at the weekend due to their actions in Gaza

The match came against a backdrop of ongoing and increasingly volatile disagreement between the two countries about Israel's military offensive in Gaza.

In May 2024, Ireland officially recognised a Palestinian state – alongside Spain and Norway – and later that year joined South Africa's Gaza genocide case against Israel in the International Court of Justice.

The country has also refused to take part in Eurovision since 2026 due to Israel's ongoing participation in the song contest and was the first EU nation to boycott goods from illegal Israeli settlements in the West Bank.

In June, the country issued travel bans on Israeli government ministers Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich.

The war began on October 7, 2023, when Hamas-led terrorists invaded Israel, killing some 1,200 people, mostly civilians, and taking 251 others hostage.

Sports.title: Arsenal dealt ANOTHER injury blow as Christos Tzolis is forced off in Greece's clash with Netherlands just days after Kai Havertz suffered the same fate
Sports.content:
Arsenal dealt ANOTHER injury blow as Christos Tzolis is forced off in Greece's clash with Netherlands just days after Kai Havertz suffered the same fate

Arsenal have suffered yet another injury blow during the international break, with Christos Tzolis forced off with an apparent leg injury while playing for Greece.

The winger left the field in the 18th minute of his side's clash with the Netherlands with his shirt covering his face, and Gunners fans now face a nervous wait to discover the severity of the issue.

It comes a matter of days after first-choice Arsenal striker Kai Havertz was also injured against the Dutch.

Havertz was tasked with leading the line in Jurgen Klopp's first match as Germany's new head coach, and lasted just 30 minutes of the fixture with the forward having gone down appearing to signal an issue with his hamstring.

Havertz's issue emerged just minutes after he had fallen victim to a poor challenge from Quinten Timber, the brother of Havertz's Arsenal team-mate Jurrien.

Timber had arrived late for a challenge and caught Havertz high on his knee, with the German attacker immediately falling to the pitch.

Arsenal have suffered another injury blow, with Christos Tzolis picking up a leg injury while playing for Greece against the Netherlands

It comes just days after Kai Havertz was injured while facing the same side with Germany

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta could now be without two of his first-choice front three for the return of Premier League action next weekend, when the champions will take on Brighton.

Bukayo Saka, the first-choice right winger, is in the England squad and could feature in the Three Lions' games against Croatia and the Czech Republic.

Declan Rice had already withdrawn from England duty with an injury, while Arteta is also currently without Cristhian Mosquera, Ben White and William Saliba.

Captain Martin Odegaard left Norway's defeat by Portugal on Sunday with a foot issue, sparking more concern, but returned to the side for their game against Wales.

Tzolis has started all five of Arsenal's Premier League games so far, making eight appearances in all competitions – picking up four assists.

Sports.title: Disgraced Team USA gymnastics doctor Larry Nassar is quietly REMOVED from Michigan sex offender registry
Sports.content:
Disgraced Team USA gymnastics doctor Larry Nassar has been quietly removed from the Michigan Sex Offender Registry list.

Nassar, who served as team doctor for the national gymnastics team from 1996 to 2014, used his position to exploit hundreds of young athletes, including medal-winning Olympic gymnasts Simone Biles and Aly Raisman.

He is currently serving multiple prison sentences lasting decades after being convicted on multiple counts of sexual abuse and child pornography in both federal and state court.

According to the Eaton County (Michigan) Prosecutor's Office, the 63-year-old is among more than 20,000 people whose names have been removed from the sex offender list after the Michigan State Police recently purged thousands of individuals from the database whose crimes happened before July 1, 2011.

A Michigan Supreme Court ruling on September 9 said that amendments to the Sex offender Registration Act issued in 2021 cannot be used to retroactively require registration due to older incidents, leading to the purge of the database.

The prosecutor's office wrote on social media that: 'The Michigan Supreme Court's decision to eliminate SORA requirements for these offenders is deeply concerning. Our community, along with the victims of these crimes, expected the registry to provide a measure of protection and awareness—assurances that have now been removed by the Court's ruling.'

Larry Nasser has been quietly removed from the Michigan Sex Offenders Registry List

Nasser is serving decades in prison after being convicted of multiple crimes

The registry is intended to 'assist the public' with preventing future criminal sexual acts by convicted sex offenders, according to Michigan State Police, and typically lists a legal name, photo, primary address, work address, age, physical description and court with records relevant to the criminal conviction.

'His conduct occurred before 2011 despite his convictions coming after,' said The Eaton County Prosecutor's Office, confirming Nasser's removal, per CBS News.

The prosecutor's office claimed the Supreme Court could have applied for a different interpretation and allowed for certain sex offenders to stay on the list.

More than 150 gymnasts were abused by Nassar during his 30-year career. Nassar admitted to sexually assaulting the athletes when he worked at Michigan State University and USA Gymnastics.

The doctor also admitted to possessing child pornography, and more than 100 women sought over $1billion from the federal government for the FBI's failure to stop him.

He was sentenced in federal court in 2017 to 60 years in prison on charges of possessing child sex abuse material. The following year, Nassar was sentenced to up to 175 years and up to 125 years, respectively, in two separate Michigan courts for molesting female gymnasts under his care.

Following the federal sentencing, U.S. Attorney Birge said: 'Today was a day of reckoning for Larry Nassar. He more than deserves this punishment for what he did.

'He consumed child pornography on a massive scale. We found 37,000 images of child pornography on his computers. Insatiable hunger of that nature simply encourages those who produce such images to continue to sexually exploit children. Compounding his danger to the public,

'Nassar was an insidious hands-on child predator in his own right. He took advantage of family friendships. And he treated his license to practice medicine as a license to sexually molest children. Thanks to the brave victims who came forward, we learned the full scope of his depravity. The breadth and dark depth of his heinous acts are extraordinary.'

Larry Nassar is pictured in court during his sentencing hearing in Michigan in January 2018

Olympic icon Simone Biles was among Nasser's long list of hundreds of victims

In April 2024, the US Justice Department announced a $138.7 million settlement with more than 100 people who accused the FBI of grossly mishandling allegations of sexual assault against Nassar in 2015 and 2016, a critical time gap that allowed the sports doctor to continue to prey on victims before his arrest.

When combined with other settlements, $1billion now has been set aside by various organizations to compensate hundreds of women who said Nassar assaulted them under the guise of treatment for sports injuries.

Simone Biles publicly broke her silence in January 2018, revealing in a powerful tweet that she was one of Nassar's victims.

'It took me a long time to write that, probably a couple of days, because every time I would go to write, I would start balling, and I couldn't get through it,' she said.

Biles also noted that she was heartbroken over having to continue to train at the ranch, the former USA Gymnastics national training center where she and her teammates were abused by the disgraced doctor.

Sports.title: Bungling Andy Burnham is criticised for ANOTHER error in attempting to clarify his statement on Man City case after being called out for 'tone-deaf' response following 'concern' over losing Abu Dhabi owners
Sports.content:
Bungling Andy Burnham is criticised for ANOTHER error in attempting to clarify his statement on Man City case after being called out for 'tone-deaf' response following 'concern' over losing Abu Dhabi owners

Prime Minister Andy Burnham has received further backlash after Number 10 attempted to clarify his comments around the financial case surrounding Manchester City.

Burnham's claim that he would be 'really concerned' if Manchester City's owners were to sell the club after it was found guilty of serious breaches of the Premier League's financial regulations has been hit by widespread criticism.

The Prime Minister made the comments following confirmation from the league that Man City had been found to have created a slew of 'sham' deals and contracts which misled the Premier League over £900million-plus in sponsorship deals over a nine-year period.

'As the Prime Minister made clear, the initial judgement is serious and there can't be any suggestion that anyone is above the rules,' a spokesperson said on Thursday. 'He also stressed that it is an ongoing independent process. It is essential that it is allowed to run its course and the outcome respected.

'If wrongdoing is established, those responsible should face the appropriate consequences.'

Football fans, though, haven't taken kindly to the latest message.

'Wrongdoing has already been established,' one fan posted on X. 'Get them gone.'

Another shared: 'This is an equally bad statement. Wrongdoing has already been established.'

A third posted: 'Burnham is a joke. We all heard what he said. He's backtracking, not clarifying.'

The end of the statement was later changed to: 'Wherever wrongdoing is established...'

Andy Burnham (with Man City chairman Khaldoon Al-Mubarak in 2019) has been criticised for comments made on his 'concern' that the club's ownership might sell

The Premier League's chief executive Richard Masters stated that the club had 'systematically broken' the rules for nearly a decade and called the decision by the Independent Commission who heard the case 'the most significant in Premier League history'.

Since confirmation of the decision broke on Tuesday evening, there have been calls for Man City to face relegation, fines, and even expulsion from the top flight, as well as arguments that the Abu Dhabi ownership group should move on – but former mayor of Greater Manchester Burnham took a more hesitant tone and lingered on the investment they had made into both the club and the city.

Those on social media were quick to suggest that Burnham's comments could likely interfere with the process of both Man City's appeal and potential future sanctions if the charges are upheld.

One fan posted: 'It was a confusing and, at best, tone-deaf intervention. Coming from a skilled operator, it was quite jarring.'

Stan Collymore suggested that Burnham's 'concern' was 'tone deaf', highlighting the 'clunky' comments as an example of the power of sports-washing.

'For a PM, the day after a judgement by a respected panel to say 'we can't afford to lose City Group, they've put a lot into Manchester' is missing the point so widely that he's now going to be tagged as taking a side or grossly naïve,' he wrote in a lengthy post on X. 'Neither things people will readily vote for.'

Rio Ferdinand added that he thought Burnham was 'on the back foot referencing Manchester City', but other commenters on the site were more critical.

'This is political interference,' one wrote. 'Already stating that he sees them as a positive influence and not wanting them gone. Unacceptable interference by influencing the (government's Football) Regulator.'

Another added: 'Absolutely disgusting statement from the PM. He's basically saying you can cheat the system all you want if you pay enough. Just shows what sort of morals he really has'.

Green Party deputy leader Mothin Ali also weighed in, saying: 'Andy Burnham's comments are staggering, just one day after saying people should come before profit, he sides with big money over the integrity of a sport that belongs to the people.

'It's a shame the prime minister appears to agree there should be one rule for the rich and one for everyone else.'

Conservative MP Louie French, who serves as shadow minister for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport warned: 'Burnham's clumsy comments haven't just undermined the ongoing legal process and Premier League. He's left the IFR Chief, who is a Labour donor and will determine the fit and proper owner test, exposed to future legal challenges, as we warned would happen.'

Burnham has received backlash for his comments as a statement trying to clarify what he said was released

Burnham's comments did attract praise from one corner of social media, with Man City supporter and Oasis frontman Liam Gallagher writing: 'There's only 1 ANDY BURNHAM.'

Burnham, whose mayoral tenure in Greater Manchester began three years after the 2014 deal struck between Manchester Council and the Abu Dhabi United Group worth £1billion promising a regeneration of city centre districts New Islington and Ancoats, had stressed in his remarks that he was unable to 'intervene' in the ongoing case.

Speaking at the home of his side Everton at the Hill Dickinson Stadium, he said: 'I would be really concerned to lose (Man City's Abu Dhabi owners).

'They've been such a huge partner in the building of modern Manchester and obviously the building of Manchester City into the global force that it is.

'I can't intervene more in the process. It would be wrong for me to do that. It would be wrong, I think, to jump to a conclusion before having really studied all of the detail, but obviously it's ongoing, and because it's still contested by Manchester City, then I think it's right that I don't say much more.'

'I do actually thank the City Football Group and the wider ownership for the money that they didn't just put into the Etihad (Stadium) and the campus around it but also into the city.'

In 2023, when charges were first brought against Man City, Abu Dhabi warned the United Kingdom that a negative outcome might damage relations with the country.

Man City have until October 2 to appeal the verdict, and Evertonian Burnham added that he did not want to assume guilt, as some had done in the wake of the Toffees' own sanctions in 2023.

'Everton was in this position a few years ago and you might remember that I fought for Everton in that situation because I still hold the view very firmly that they weren't fairly treated in that process,' he continued.

'I remember people proclaiming Everton guilty at the time and with hindsight I think more people would say that wasn't fair, the way that was handled.

'So it would be wrong of me to leap to one side given the experience that I'd had before becoming prime minister.'

Everton had fallen foul of the Premier League's financial regulations and were charged and deducted ten points, later reduced to six on appeal. But this was the scenario Man City seem to have been looking to avoid during the 2009-18 period scrutinised by the Independent Commission.

David Kogan, chairman of the Independent Football Regulator (IFR), stated that he had the powers to 'assess the suitability of owners, directors and executive' and that the body would look to use their powers to protect 'the sustainability, honesty and integrity of English football'.

The IFR and the FA will assess the findings once the sanctioning and appeals process has been completed.

Man City continue to deny any wrongdoing, with chief executive Ferran Soriano stating in a video shared with the club's staff that they were in possession of 'irrefutable evidence' of their innocence that could dispel the Premier League's 'conspiracy theory' on appeal.

Sports.title: Second Hull City star crashes on his way to training - in almost the EXACT same spot as team-mate who flipped his £160,000 Land Rover Defender three weeks ago
Sports.content:
A second Hull City player has crashed their car on the way to training, just three weeks after their team-mate Sorba Thomas flipped his vehicle. A Mercedes was pictured on its side on a residential road close to the Premier League club's training ground. The identity of the player remains unknown, but midfielder Lucas Gourna-Douath posed for a photograph with the car in question in an Instagram post on Wednesday. In a statement, the club said: 'Hull City is aware of images circulating on social media following a road traffic accident near the club’s training ground and can confirm that no one was harmed in the incident.' Humberside Police have confirmed emergency services responded to an incident and that no-one was injured. 'Officers and emergency services were called to reports of a single vehicle road traffic collision on Millhouse Woods Lane in Cottingham at around 8.30am this morning (Thursday, 1 October 2026). 'Thankfully, no one was injured as a result of the collision.' A second Hull City player has crashed their car close to the Premier League club's training ground The identity of the player remains unknown, but midfielder Lucas Gourna-Douath posed for a photograph with the car in question in an Instagram post on Wednesday

Your browser does not support iframes.

Gourna-Douath, who signed for the Tigers in a £3million move from RB Salzburg in the summer, had recently received the new vehicle. 'Another one! 2026 GLC 53 sourced for Lucas Gourna,' the post read. 'Thank you for your order.' The incident comes three weeks after Thomas flipped his Land Rover on the way to training. The 27-year-old walked away from the crash, which happened on Millhouse Woods Lane in Cottingham at around 8.30am. His vehicle, a grey Land Rover Defender with a personalised number plate, was pictured on its roof, with broken windows. Residents had looked on stunned at the crash on the narrow road, where locals say speeds typically only hit 15mph. Thomas escaped injury in the crash and came off the bench for Hull the following day in their 2-2 draw against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge.

Sports.title: Erling Haaland is SUING a Norwegian airline after they launched a World Cup advert with a plane sporting his ponytail haircut
Sports.content:
Erling Haaland is SUING a Norwegian airline after they launched a World Cup advert with a plane sporting his ponytail haircut

Manchester City forward Erling Haaland is suing a Norwegian airline for using a plane with his signature hairstyle in an advert.

Haaland, who cut his hair at the start of the season, became synonymous with his ponytail hair that he donned while scoring plenty of goals for both club and country.

Airline Norwegian Air Shuttle ASA used an image during the World Cup of a plane with Haaland's hair edited onto it, and the forward has failed to see the funny side of things.

The caption read: 'We've never felt more Norwegian.'

The post has since been deleted from the company's social media channels.

Haaland is now taking the company to court with allegations of a violation of the Marketing Act, and, on October 9, a meeting between the judge and lawyers before the main hearing will take place, according to Norwegian publication VG.

Erling Haaland is suing a Norwegian airline after they used his haircut for an 

Company spokesperson Catharina Solli said: 'We struggle to understand why we have been taken to court. Just like almost everyone else in Norway, we encouraged the national team during the summer.

'We did this by publishing a few things spontaneously, inspired by social media trends.

'It is unfortunate that this encouragement has been greeted by a lawsuit. But we hope to have a reasonable dialogue, in order that we can continue in the future to support our sporting heroes together.'

Haaland's lawyer Thomas Hagen, meanwhile, said: 'This case is about the illegal use by Norwegian of Haaland's distinguishing features to sell air tickets during the World Cup finals.'

Haaland scored seven goals as Norway made it to the quarter-finals in their first World Cup this century before losing to England.

Sports.title: Revealed: Cristiano Ronaldo could be slapped with a six-month BAN after walking out on Portugal - as the country's prime minister reveals talks with the 'betrayed' 41-year-old star
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo could be facing a ban of up to six months from the Portugal national team after sensationally storming out of the team's training camp amid a row with manager Jorge Jesus.

The star, 41, landed in Madrid in the early hours of Thursday morning after flying from Copenhagen, where Portugal are due to face Denmark, on his private jet.

He had been seen leaving the Parken Stadium in the Danish capital on Wednesday after missing a third consecutive training session.

Ronaldo later confirmed in a statement on Instagram that he had left the team's camp because of comments made by Jesus in his press conference.

The Portugal boss said the captain would not start the Denmark clash, just days after sitting on the bench for the entirety of the 2-1 win in Norway, but insisted there was no issue between the two.

And reports in Portugal claim Ronaldo could be suspended from playing for his country for between one and six months if he is found to have 'abandoned' the team.

Cristiano Ronaldo (left) sensationally walked out on Portugal amid a dispute with his manager

The Portuguese Football Federation's disciplinary code states: 'Any player who, having been regularly called up, unjustifiably abandons or fails to appear for training, a match, or any activity of the national teams or related to the sporting representation of the FPF or Portugal, will be sanctioned with a suspension of one to six months.'

Ronaldo said: 'After the national team coach's press conference, and following a conversation with the President of the Portuguese Football Federation, I have decided to leave the national team training camp.

'In due time, I will tell all Portuguese people the truth about the reasons that led to my departure from the national team, to which I have always dedicated myself.

'Now is the time to wish good luck to Portugal and to all my teammates.'

Ronaldo's decision to quit the Portuguese camp has sparked suggestions he may retire from international duty and has even prompted the intervention of the country's Prime Minister, Luís Montenegro.

Record reports Montenegro has discussed the issue with Ronaldo, as well as Jesus and Pedro Proenca, the head of the Portuguese FA.

It is unclear whether Montenegro was attempting to resolve a dispute described as an 'earthquake' in Portugal, or if he was merely wanting to be briefed.

Speaking before the Denmark game, Jesus insisted he had a 'completely' clear conscience amid the Ronaldo saga. 'It was a frantic few hours because we had two games,' he added.

'Now we have another one... Besides, I've been in football for many years and I know I didn't do anything to prevent the situation from continuing as before.'

Footage published by A Bola showed Jesus and Proenca being booed by a small group of fans who had gathered outside the team's hotel in Copenhagen before the team made the short journey to Parken Stadium.

Reports in Portugal claim the dispute in the national team camp has reached Prime Minister Luis Montenegro

Ronaldo's sister Elma has come out in support of her brother after his shock exit from the Portugal camp (Source: Elma_Official/Instagram)

Ronaldo's sister, Elma Aveiro, had earlier fanned the flames of controversy by claiming Portuguese people 'deserve mediocrity' because of their treatment of the country's record goalscorer.

'The national team deserved better structuring,' she wrote on Instagram. 'The Portuguese press deserved more competence and fewer guesses.

'As for the Portuguese... well, they don't deserve the best in anything. We are envious, contemptuous, ignorant, and we deserve to return to the mediocrity we always had in football before CR7. Thank you for everything CR7!'

Elma was not the only supporter from inside Ronaldo's camp to suggest that the five-time Ballon d'Or winner had been treated unfairly, with Spanish journalist Edu Aguirre - who is friends with the Al-Nassr superstar - claiming he had been 'betrayed' by Jesus.

'There was a meeting yesterday, Tuesday night,' he told Spanish programme El Chiringuito. 'A meeting between the Federation president, the coach, and Cristiano. Jorge Jesus apologized to Cristiano for the disregard shown in making him warm up for 30 minutes instead of playing him.

'And not only did he apologize privately, but he also told him he would apologize publicly, that he would publicly admit his mistake. That's Jorge Jesus's promise to Cristiano. And then he goes to the press conference and tells this many lies that nobody believes.

'That's why Cristiano explodes, because he feels betrayed. There's nothing more to it, it's really like that. Your coach comes to you privately: "Look, see, this is how it was, you understand me, okay, I didn't manage the situation well, we're in this together, I'm sorry. If there's a press conference, I'll clarify everything, I'll apologize, don't worry, everything will be fine, everything will be resolved." Then you go to the press conference 12 hours later and leave Cristiano still...

'Worse, you're acting tough, saying that you're the one in charge and that Cristiano is just another player. Go home and move on. That's why I say: betrayal.'

Ronaldo confirmed on Wednesday night that he had left the camp amid a row with Jorge Jesus

The captain confirmed he had withdrawn from the squad because of Jesus's comments

Ronaldo held talks with Jesus and Proenca on Wednesday morning, a meeting initially described as amicable.

But the rift between Ronaldo and his manager appeared to deepen after Jesus's press conference.

Jesus admitted Ronaldo had been 'angry' with him, with footage showing the captain walking off down the tunnel after sitting out the victory in Norway.

Jesus, who also worked with Ronaldo at Al-Nassr, said: 'There was no incident whatsoever.

'Any player - and I was a player myself - when you spend 20 or 30 minutes warming up and then don't get on, no-one is happy about that.

'Afterwards, as coach, I decided not to bring him on. It's nothing to make a fuss about.'

Jesus also suggested Goncalo Ramos would keep his place in the side ahead of Ronaldo for the Denmark match. 'If I need [Ronaldo], he'll come on,' he said. 'If I don't need him, he won't.'

Jesus had originally planned to bring on the veteran striker for a 30-minute cameo but then decided to leave him on the bench, which has seemingly sparked the feud.

It is an inauspicious start to the relationship between Jesus and Ronaldo, who opted not to retire from international duty after the World Cup.

Only a week ago, Ronaldo reiterated his commitment to the cause, saying: 'I had a conversation with our president, with our coach (about his future).

'I still believe that I'm able to help the national team to reach what they want, and will finish when I feel like I'm not doing anything here.

'I think I can give to the national team my support, not only through the goals, but also outside of football.

'This is a new young generation. But for me the basic point is to be able on the pitch to score the goals and to help the team win games.'

Ronaldo will turn 42 in February and has scored three goals in five games for Al-Nassr so far in the Saudi Pro League this season.

Sports.title: Jurgen Klopp erupts over 'complete nonsense' as ex-Liverpool boss left raging
Sports.content:
Jurgen Klopp erupts over 'complete nonsense' as ex-Liverpool boss left raging

Germany boss Jurgen Klopp has furiously criticised criticism of his national side by far-right politicians ahead of their match with Serbia in the Nations League

View 2 Images Jurgen Klopp has called the debate 'idiocy' (Image: Alexander Hassenstein/Getty Images)

Jurgen Klopp has labelled the debate over whether his Germany team are 'German enough' or 'white enough' as idiocy. The former Liverpool boss refused to engage in the conversation and suggested there is no reason to pay attention to the people starting it.

‌



‌



Klopp, 59, signed a four-year deal as Germany boss over the summer and is now conducting his first camp in charge of the team. He has got off to a slow start with Die Mannschaft drawing with the Netherlands and losing to Greece during his spell in charge so far.

‌



The defeat on Sunday has seen a number of far-right politicians attack the team for the few white players included. In one post, Kay Gottschalk, the deputy leader of Alternative für Deutschland (AfD), reshared side-by-side images of West Germany’s team from the 1990 World Cup final with the team Klopp selected to face Greece.

‌



In the 1990 image, all of the players were white, while the team that played in Augsburg included eight non-white players. Quoting that post, Gottschalk said: “Character traits, certain virtues, and team spirit are cultural values that develop over centuries and are shaped by shared historical experiences.”

Asked to respond, Klopp hit out. “There is absolutely no reason to pay attention to these people," he said.

‌



"You won’t get my thoughts on this. I have little time in everyday life for idiocy – and even less on social media.

“The great crux of our lives is that everyone is allowed to express their opinion … it’s insane when something like that exists.”

Klopped added that he believes mutual respect is still possible. “The world could learn a thing or two from a sports changing room … There, everyone is respected based on the facts and not discredited based on false opinions," he said.

‌



View 2 Images Jurgen Klopp was unhappy with the line of questioning (Image: Alexander Hassenstein/Getty Images)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

The last decade has seen similar lines of attack from the AfD. In 2016, following Germany's European Championship elimination, Beatrix von Storch, the AfD’s Deputy Party Leader, wrote on X that “Perhaps the German NATIONAL TEAM should play again next time?"

‌



After taking the reins for the national side, Klopp has advocated for 'positive patriotism' and wants to reclaim the German flag. Speaking last month, he said: “I don’t want to entrust national pride to the wrong people.

"A crazy amount of things have happened not that long ago. There was a vote which some people probably found OK, but others would have thought: ‘Good heavens, what’s going on here?’

“From the perspective of someone in sport, I’d like to reclaim the flag for myself and for us. When we wave it, I don’t want that someone thinks: ‘What’s going on with you?’ I want that they think you’re happy and you understand how lucky you are to be born in this wonderful country or to have moved here and live here.”

Sports.title: Newcastle United fans inspire a new £115,000 stadium deep in the heart of Africa
Sports.content:
Newcastle United fans inspire a new £115,000 stadium deep in the heart of Africa

EXCLUSIVE: FIFA made its first-ever grant to Zambia after fundraising by an intrepid Tyneside couple - we first told the story of Crispin Mason-Jones and his wife, Dr Ellie Bond, in 2022

View 4 Images Members of the Mfuwe Mags U15s try out their new kit - and it resembles Newcasle's famous trim (Image: Andy Commins / Daily Mirror)

A new stadium inspired by Newcastle United fans will soon be built deep in the heart of Africa.

‌



‌



FIFA made its first-ever grant to Zambia after years of fundraising and campaigning by an intrepid Tyneside couple - backed by the Daily Mirror.

‌



We first told the story of Crispin Mason-Jones, 64, and his wife, Dr Ellie Bond, 60, in 2022.

‌



We travelled with them to the rural community of Mfuwe to see the first kit delivered to a team known as the 'Mfuwe Mags,' inspired by the couple's love of Newcastle United.

Now Crispin's plans for a new pitch at the 'JK Stadium' in the bush are taking shape with a £115,000 ($150,000) grant from FIFA, the first ever awarded to the African country.

The exciting development will be built alongside a multi-sport facility and an educational outreach project.

‌



Crispin, 64, of Jesmond, Newcastle, said: "The grant is to go towards the cost of the main football pitch and the all-weather multi-sport facility.

View 4 Images The plans for the new pitch in Mfuwe, Zambia

"The Zambian currency may have dropped in value since last year but it will still go a long way toward achieving our goals."

‌



He added: "It is for the region's people.

"The educational buildings on the site were through our joint venture with the Project Luangwa Foundation.

"They are now completed and were instrumental in us receiving the grant from FIFA.

‌



"We would not have received the grant without the new buildings.

The exciting plans and the transformation of the land are show in the designs for the new stadium - and the work that has already been done on the ground.

Aerial shots show the bare land transformed with areas marked out for the new football pitch and a vital all-weather facility.

‌



Crispin is now looking at options to ship both strips and Astroturf out to Africa from the UK, and fundraising for the transport costs.

View 4 Images Plans for the new football development in Zambia are shown by these aerial photographs

"We are now focusing on providing kit to schools rather than local teams to foster sport within them.

‌



"I did the original drawings and the early work with Project Luangwa, and I am now looking for Astroturf for the pitch."

Apart from the Mags, The Valley Queens, who play in the Zambian National League, will also benefit from the work done by Project Luangwa at the JK Stadium.

The Mirror joined Crispin as he brought £1,000 worth of black-and-white strips and 21 pairs of junior football boots to the Mags under-15 side.

‌



View 4 Images The children of Zambia in their new kit

They have provided thousands more kits since then, taking them over 5,000 miles from Tyneside to Africa.

Project Luangwa has another Toon supporter in CEO Ian Macallan. Originally from Durham, he provided education at remote bush schools alongside health and sporting programmes.

‌



Toon fan Ian, chief operating officer of Project Luangwa, works with communities in the area on tourism, education and gender programmes.

In July, it was awarded a $150,000 grant from Fifa's Global Citizen Education Fund to develop sporting opportunities in Mfuwe.

It is the first time Zambia has received a Fifa grant of this kind. The money is intended to provide facilities including a football pitch and facilities for tennis, basketball and netball.
