World.title: Bryan Ruiz Debuts as Costa Rica Coach With Nations League Survival at Stake
World.content:
Bryan Ruiz will coach Costa Rica’s national soccer team for the first time tonight when La Sele visits Nicaragua in a Concacaf Nations League match that could decide whether Costa Rica stays in the competition’s top tier. Kickoff is at 8 p.m. Costa Rica time (10 p.m. ET) at Nicaragua’s National Stadium in Managua.

The former captain takes over at one of the lowest points in the team’s recent history. Costa Rica opened its League A, Group A campaign with a 4-3 home loss to Curaçao and a 2-0 defeat to Haiti, leaving it without a point after two matches. Those results ended the tenure of Argentine coach Fernando “Bocha” Batista, who left after seven months without a win. The Costa Rican Football Federation (FCRF) turned to Ruiz to lead the team, initially for the final two matches of the group stage.

Costa Rica sits fifth in the group, ahead of only Nicaragua and behind Curaçao, Haiti, the Dominican Republic and Trinidad and Tobago. Tonight’s match pits the two bottom teams against each other. Costa Rica no longer controls its own fate. The team needs to beat Nicaragua tonight and Haiti at home on Sunday just to keep alive its hopes of avoiding relegation to League B.

The slide has also hit Costa Rica in the global standings. La Sele dropped six places to 57th in FIFA’s live ranking after the two losses, and it has not won two matches in a row since June 2025. Ruiz made four changes to Batista’s last squad. Goalkeeper Keylor Navas, midfielder Celso Borges, defender Juan Pablo Vargas and Roan Wilson return, while Gerald Taylor, Sebastián Padilla, Gian Mauro Morera and Mathías Elizondo were left out.

The return of Navas and Borges reunites Ruiz with two teammates from the 2014 World Cup squad that reached the quarterfinals in Brazil, the best finish in the country’s history. Ruiz has named Wílmer López and Edson Soto as his assistants. Speaking at his final press conference before the team traveled to Managua, Ruiz said he had not been seeking the national team job and had not rushed anything, noting that he has spent four years preparing as a coach.

He said Navas remains the best goalkeeper Costa Rica has and should stay with the team for as long as he wants to. Navas, for his part, described the appointment as a good opportunity for his former captain. Ruiz led only four training sessions before tonight’s match. Analysts have cautioned that such a short window leaves little room for deep tactical changes.

This is the first meeting between Costa Rica and Nicaragua in the Nations League. When the two sides last met in Nicaragua, during qualifying for the 2026 World Cup, the match ended 1-1. In Costa Rica, the match will be broadcast exclusively on Fox. Costa Rica closes the group stage against Haiti at home on Sunday.

World.title: Costa Rica Extradites Alleged Meth Ringleader to Florida
World.content:
Costa Rican authorities moved Farid Alberto Morales Araya, known as “Beto,” from La Reforma prison to Juan Santamaría International Airport early today as they prepared to hand him over to U.S. authorities to face federal drug trafficking charges in Florida. Morales Araya, 40, is tied to a May 2025 operation in which Costa Rican police seized 48 kilograms (106 pounds) of crystal methamphetamine in Tibás. At the time, authorities described it as the largest synthetic drug seizure in Costa Rica’s history.

Morales Araya is wanted by the U.S. District Court for the Middle District of Florida on drug trafficking allegations. Four other men wanted by the same court are being surrendered with him. The Ministry of Public Security carried out today’s operation at the request of the Attorney General’s Office and in coordination with the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration, or DEA.

The heavily guarded convoy left the maximum-security Centro de Alta Contención, part of the La Reforma prison complex in Alajuela, at about 6:15 a.m. It arrived minutes later at Base 2 of Costa Rica’s Air Surveillance Service at Juan Santamaría International Airport. A U.S. aircraft was waiting while Costa Rican authorities completed migration, judicial and handover procedures. Those steps can take several hours before the men are formally transferred to U.S. agents and flown out of the country.

Authorities stressed that extradition does not amount to a conviction. All five men will have the opportunity to answer the allegations against them before the federal court in Florida. The case against Morales Araya began after the DEA shared information with Costa Rican prosecutors and the Drug Control Police, known as the PCD, about a group allegedly using Costa Rica as a transit point for methamphetamine headed toward North America.

Undercover officers first arranged the purchase of 1 kilogram (2.2 pounds) of crystal methamphetamine for $3,800. Investigators then negotiated a much larger delivery involving another 48 kilograms (106 pounds). Police moved in when the suspects attempted to complete that transaction in May 2025.

Officers intercepted two vehicles. One, stopped in Tibás, was allegedly being used to conceal the drugs. Morales Araya and Colombian national José Franklin Cuesta were detained in another vehicle in San Francisco de Dos Ríos. Investigators identify Morales Araya as the alleged leader of the group and the person who negotiated its drug transactions. Cuesta, who is also being extradited today, allegedly handled logistics.

A third man arrested during the same Costa Rican operation is not included in the U.S. extradition request. The United States formally requested Morales Araya’s extradition on December 19, 2025, while he was already being held in pretrial detention in Costa Rica. The San José Criminal Court approved his extradition on August 14. The decision became final when no appeal was filed. Before Costa Rica could hand him over, U.S. authorities were required to provide several guarantees.

Those include assurances that Morales Araya will not face the death penalty, life imprisonment or a prison sentence longer than Costa Rica’s 50-year maximum. He may also only be prosecuted for the crimes covered by the extradition request. The other three men being transferred today are wanted by the same Florida court in a separate cocaine trafficking case. They are Andrés Felipe Restrepo Uribe, 51, a Colombian-born naturalized Costa Rican; Luis Alberto Sinisterra Lozano; and Yon Fredy Sánchez Chavarro.

The three were arrested in June 2025 in central San José, near Paseo Colón, during an operation in which authorities reported finding 70 kilograms (154 pounds) of cocaine. According to U.S. investigators, they allegedly operated a network that moved large quantities of cocaine from Costa Rica toward North America, with Restrepo Uribe accused of supplying the drugs. The United States formally requested their extradition in September 2025.

Today’s transfer is the latest in a series of high-profile extraditions since Costa Rica amended its Constitution in 2025 to allow the surrender of its own citizens in international drug trafficking and terrorism cases. Former Supreme Court magistrate Celso Gamboa and Edwin López, alias “Pecho de Rata,” were sent to Texas. Johnny Angulo, alias “John Cadenas,” was extradited to Italy. In August, Gilbert Bell, alias “Macho Coca,” and Gabriel Lozano, alias “Compadre,” were sent to New York.

Other extradition cases are still moving through Costa Rican courts. Jordie Picado Grijalba, alias “Noni,” described by authorities as an alleged second-in-command of a southern Caribbean drug trafficking group, is awaiting the resolution of a criminal case in Costa Rica before he can be surrendered. Iván Javier Pablot Martínez has been cleared for extradition to France.

Costa Rican courts are also processing dozens of extradition requests in drug cases, while a separate proposal to widen extradition of Costa Rican citizens remains pending. Once today’s handover is completed, Morales Araya and the other four men will enter U.S. custody and face the cases filed against them in Florida.

World.title: Costa Rica Braces for Afternoon Storms as Tropical Wave No. 48 Arrives
World.content:
Tropical Wave No. 48 is expected to cross Costa Rica today bringing a greater chance of afternoon downpours and thunderstorms as already wet areas face an increased risk of flooding and landslides. The National Meteorological Institute (IMN) said a drop in atmospheric pressure across Central America is pulling the Intertropical Convergence Zone (the band near the equator where trade winds meet, creating clouds, storms and frequent heavy rain) closer to Costa Rica.

Combined with the tropical wave, that will increase atmospheric instability over the country and help fuel rainfall through Thursday and into the coming days. The day is expected to begin relatively calm and much of Costa Rica will see partly cloudy skies and warm, muggy conditions during the morning before the weather changes during the afternoon.

The IMN expects showers and thunderstorms to develop first around the mountains and higher elevations. Rain could then spread into lower parts of the Greater Metropolitan Area (GMA), the Northern areas and the Caribbean. In the Central Valley, San José, Alajuela, Cartago and Heredia are forecast to remain partly cloudy during the morning before scattered afternoon downpours and thunderstorms develop.

Cloudy conditions, isolated rain and patches of fog could linger into Thursday night. San José is expected to reach about 28°C (83°F), while Alajuela could climb to 31°C (88°F). Cartago will be cooler at around 25°C (77°F), with Heredia near 29°C (84°F). The North Pacific will also see a hot morning followed by scattered thunderstorms during the afternoon. Liberia could reach around 36°C (96°F), while Puntarenas is also forecast near 36°C. Nicoya could reach approximately 35°C (94°F).

In the Central and South Pacific, rainfall is expected mainly around mountainous areas during the afternoon, with variable cloud cover continuing into the evening. Quepos is forecast to reach about 33°C (91°F), while Golfito could reach 34°C (93°F). The Northern Zone and Caribbean could also see afternoon thunderstorms, particularly near the mountains, followed by scattered rain into the evening. Ciudad Quesada is forecast near 28°C (82°F), while Limón could reach around 30°C (85°F). Of particular concern are areas where the ground is already saturated after recent rainfall.

In its latest weather advisor from yesterday, the IMN reported soil saturation above 95% in parts of the Northern Zone and Northern Caribbean, as well as areas near the mountains of the Central and South Pacific. The institute warned that additional rainfall could increase the possibility of overflowing streams, drainage problems, localized flooding and landslides.

The IMN also said rainfall totals in some of the more affected areas could reach 20 to 50 millimeters, with localized totals of 60 to 80 millimeters. In other parts of the Central Valley, rainfall totals of 5 to 30 millimeters were possible. Anyone in that part of Costa Rica should use extra caution in areas prone to flooding and landslides, particularly during the afternoon and evening. The IMN also recommends seeking shelter during thunderstorms and remaining alert for strong wind gusts near storm cells.

The wetter pattern may continue beyond today. The IMN’s weekly outlook through October 4 calls for humid and unstable conditions, with the Central Pacific and mountainous parts of the Caribbean and Northern Zone carrying some of the greatest potential for moderate to heavy rain.

World.title: Costa Rica Moves to Restrict Imports Linked to Forced Labor
World.content:
Costa Rica is setting up a new system to keep goods made with forced labor from entering, a move that comes a little more than two months after the United States imposed an additional tariff on Costa Rican exports over the same issue. President Laura Fernández signed the Executive Decree, which was published in an extraordinary supplement to the official La Gaceta newspaper.

The decree orders the Ministry of Foreign Trade (COMEX) and the Ministry of Labor and Social Security (MTSS) to create and maintain a public list of goods considered at risk of being produced, extracted or manufactured, in whole or in part, using forced labor. The important point for importers is that the list does not exist yet. The two ministries now have 60 calendar days to establish the rules and criteria that will be used to build it. Hacienda, Costa Rica’s Finance Ministry, will also be involved when customs, tax or government purchasing issues come into play.

Products from any country could eventually be included. Authorities will be allowed to use reports from international organizations, investigations by foreign governments, court and administrative decisions, specialized studies and other technical information. The decree says those decisions must be based on information that is objective, verifiable and sufficient to show a risk that forced labor was used somewhere in the production process. The rules also call for avoiding arbitrary discrimination between countries facing similar circumstances.

Once the list is established, it will be published on the COMEX and Labor Ministry websites. Importers will also have a new responsibility to check the products they bring into Costa Rica. At a minimum, businesses will be expected to verify that the merchandise they are importing does not appear on the government’s forced-labor list.

If a listed product is presented for import, the appropriate Costa Rican authorities will be able to apply monitoring and control measures already available under national law. The decree itself does not mean every product placed on the list will automatically be confiscated or rejected at the border.

The rules will also reach government purchasing. Public institutions will be required to check the list when planning purchases, preparing bidding requirements, reviewing possible risks and setting contract conditions. However, a product appearing on the list will not automatically disqualify a company from a government contract. That would require support in the bidding rules, existing law or a formal administrative decision.

The new policy follows a major trade dispute with the United States. In March, the Office of the U.S. Trade Representative opened investigations into 60 economies, including Costa Rica, to determine whether they prohibited imports made with forced labor and whether those restrictions were actually enforced.

U.S. trade officials concluded in June that Costa Rica did not have an effective prohibition in place. On July 23, the USTR announced its final action, placing a 12.5% Section 301 tariff on Costa Rican goods that were not covered by exemptions. The additional duty took effect July 24.

Costa Rica had argued during the U.S. investigation that its exports should be excluded from the additional tariffs and that existing trade conditions under the CAFTA-DR free trade agreement should be preserved. The Costa Rican decree does not explicitly state that it was issued because of the U.S. tariff decision. However, it addresses the same issue identified by U.S. trade officials: the lack of a system designed to prevent goods made with forced labor from entering Costa Rica.

The U.S. tariff does not apply equally to every Costa Rican export. Washington established exemptions for a range of products when it announced the Section 301 measures. For businesses importing goods into Costa Rica, as of now the change is mainly procedural because there is not yet a published list of affected merchandise.

The more important stage will come once COMEX and the Labor Ministry establish the criteria, begin naming products and explain how the list will be updated and enforced.

World.title: Costa Rica Opens Modern Pier at Historic San Lucas Island
World.content:
Visitors to San Lucas Island National Park now have an easier way to get ashore after Costa Rica opened a new tourist pier at the former prison island in the Gulf of Nicoya. The modernized dock was inaugurated yesterday, replacing aging infrastructure at one of Puntarenas’ best-known historical and nature destinations.

President Laura Fernández attended the opening alongside Costa Rican Tourism Institute (ICT) executive president Marcos V. Borges, government officials and tourism representatives. The first visitors arrived by boat during the ceremony and stepped ashore using the new pier.

The ICT financed the project, investing more than ₡1.1 billion in the new infrastructure. Borges said the pier is intended to improve access, safety and comfort for visitors while helping strengthen tourism in Puntarenas. The dock can accommodate as many as four boats at the same time and was designed to meet the accessibility requirements of Law 7600, Costa Rica’s law protecting equal access for people with disabilities.

Sustainability was also built into the project. The pier operates entirely with solar panels and includes a rainwater collection system for use at the site. The project also received an Ecological Blue Flag award in the construction category.

Building the dock presented unusual challenges. Crews were working inside a national park and over the water, requiring additional measures to protect marine ecosystems. Weather, tides and the logistics of transporting materials to an island also complicated construction.

Officials expect the benefits to extend beyond tourists. The new infrastructure should provide better working conditions for guides, park rangers and tour operators while making it easier for more visitors to include the island in trips through Puntarenas. The ICT also sees San Lucas as part of a wider effort to bring in cruise passengers and travelers interested in the Gulf of Nicoya’s history, wildlife and natural attractions.

The project involved coordination between the ICT, the Environment Ministry, the National System of Conservation Areas, the Public Works and Transport Ministry, the park’s board and the Culture Ministry’s heritage office. San Lucas Island remained open to tourists while construction was underway.

For many visitors, the island’s history remains its biggest attraction. San Lucas served as a prison for more than a century before closing in 1991. Its abandoned buildings and prison ruins remain throughout the island and helped inspire José León Sánchez’s well-known novel “La Isla de los Hombres Solos.”

But San Lucas offers more than its prison history. Visitors can explore about 15 kilometers (9.3 miles) of trails, archaeological sites and one of the remaining tropical dry forests in Mesoamerica. Wildlife includes white-tailed deer, anteaters and howler monkeys, along with resident and migratory birds.

Costa Rica officially created San Lucas Island National Park on August 24, 2020. The island sits in the Gulf of Nicoya, a short boat trip from Puntarenas. The park is open daily from 8:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. Most visitors reach the island through guided boat tours departing from downtown Puntarenas.

For those exploring Costa Rica’s Pacific coast, the new pier removes one of the practical obstacles to visiting an island that combines national history, wildlife and some of the Gulf of Nicoya’s lesser-known scenery.

World.title: PSU objects to Troy Gabb as Acting PSC Chair, cites political commentary; appointment revives controversial DFC-era history
World.content:
PSU objects to Troy Gabb as Acting PSC Chair, cites political commentary; appointment revives controversial DFC-era history

By Breaking Belize News Staff: The Public Service Union of Belize (PSU) has formally objected to the appointment of Troy Gabb as Acting Chairperson of the Public Services Commission (PSC), saying his record as a political commentator and his past public positions raise concerns about confidence in the body responsible for appointments, promotions and discipline in the public service.

In a statement issued today, October 1, the PSU said Gabb, a weekly commentator on Love FM, has “repeatedly shown hostility toward trade unions,” opposed PSU positions on public policy and sharply criticized public officers. The Union further described him as widely perceived to be politically partisan. Those characterizations are the PSU’s stated position.

The Belize Gazette of July 23 confirms that Governor General Dame Froyla Tzalam appointed Gabb to act as Chairperson of the PSC effective July 20, 2026, while substantive Chairperson Diana Price-Murillo is on leave.

But Gabb is no stranger to controversy involving public institutions.

He previously served as Chief Executive Officer of the Development Finance Corporation (DFC) during a period that later became the subject of extensive Senate scrutiny and a Commission of Inquiry over questionable loans, securitization arrangements and other transactions at the state-owned lending institution.

During Senate hearings in 2004, Gabb was questioned about DFC’s large portfolio of non-performing loans. He acknowledged at the time that roughly 35% of DFC’s loan portfolio was non-performing, while senators questioned the institution’s due diligence surrounding major borrowers, including the Novelo’s Group.

Gabb was again called before the DFC Commission of Inquiry in 2007, where he faced questions concerning a number of major transactions, including the Novelo loans, DFC’s involvement in the Mahogany Heights deal, transactions involving companies associated with former DFC chairman Glenn Godfrey and a multimillion-dollar transaction involving the Belize Bank and Government.

One of the more personally controversial issues raised during those hearings concerned a San Pedro property Gabb acquired from DFC for $15,000. Contemporary reporting on the inquiry said commissioners placed its value at approximately $68,000, meaning the purchase price was roughly $53,000 below that valuation. Gabb was questioned about the transaction during his testimony.

The inquiry also heard testimony that, during Gabb’s tenure, certain DFC administration or legal fees were waived or varied in selected cases, with commissioners questioning what authority existed for the CEO to exercise that discretion.

Gabb defended his stewardship of the DFC and challenged aspects of the inquiry and forensic audit, arguing that adverse findings had been prepared without first allowing him an opportunity to respond and questioning the legality of the forensic auditor’s appointment.

Justice Herbert Lord’s subsequent report concluded more broadly that wrongdoing had occurred in the operations of the DFC during the period investigated. That finding concerned the institution and transactions examined by the Commission and should not, by itself, be read as a finding that Gabb personally committed a criminal offence.

Against that history, the PSU says it also opposes Gabb being reappointed as a member of the PSC when his current term expires in November 2026.

“Building a strong Public Service begins with confidence and trust in the Commission,” the Union said.

The PSU has written to Minister of the Public Service Henry Charles Usher outlining its concerns and has called for future PSC appointments to be persons with public-service knowledge, integrity and standing who command the respect of both public officers and the wider public.

The Union also extended best wishes to Price-Murillo and said it hopes for a speedy resolution of the circumstances surrounding her leave and her return to office.

World.title: Sentencing delayed again for cops convicted over filming viral sex video of couple having sex
World.content:
Sentencing delayed again for cops convicted over filming viral sex video of couple having sex

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Two police officers convicted of wilful oppression for recording and circulating a video of a couple engaged in a sexual act during the COVID-19 pandemic will have to wait a little longer to learn their fate after their sentencing was adjourned again on Thursday.

Police Corporal Jason Shaw and Police Constable Leslie Martinez appeared before High Court Justice Derick Sylvester for sentencing, but the matter could not proceed because reports previously ordered by the court were still outstanding.

Justice Sylvester therefore adjourned the matter to Monday, October 5, 2026.

Shaw and Martinez were unanimously convicted on July 17 by a nine-member jury after less than two hours of deliberation. The five women and four men on the jury found both officers guilty of wilful oppression.

The case stems from an April 5, 2020 incident in which the officers recorded a couple engaged in a sexual act inside an abandoned building in Belize City. Prosecutors said the video was subsequently shared in a police WhatsApp group known as “Loyal Group” before spreading publicly and causing humiliation to the couple.

The July proceedings were a retrial. An earlier trial ended after the jury was unable to reach the required verdict, and the matter was later transferred to Justice Sylvester.

A third police officer, Anthony Villamil, had originally been charged alongside Shaw and Martinez, but prosecutors later withdrew the charge against him and granted him immunity in exchange for his testimony.

Shaw and Martinez remain awaiting sentencing and are due back before the High Court on October 5.

World.title: Khris Rosado sentencing delayed again in fatal crash that killed Police Constable Arcenio Cus
World.content:
Khris Rosado sentencing delayed again in fatal crash that killed Police Constable Arcenio Cus

By Breaking Belize News Staff: The sentencing of businessman Khris Rosado for causing the death of Police Constable Arcenio Cus has been postponed again, this time until Monday, October 5, 2026.

Rosado appeared before High Court Justice Derick Sylvester on Thursday morning for what was expected to be his sentencing hearing, but the matter was adjourned. Justice Sylvester apologized for the delay and indicated that efforts would be made to conclude the matter at the next appearance.

Rosado, the owner of Thirsty Thursday, pleaded guilty on June 16 to causing death by careless conduct in connection with the July 28, 2025 traffic collision on the Philip Goldson Highway that claimed the life of 38-year-old PC Cus.

His sentencing had initially been scheduled for June 30 but was postponed to October 1 after his attorney, Dr. Lynden Jones, requested an adjournment because he was engaged in another matter outside the district.

Police said Cus, who was from Silver Creek Village, was travelling toward Belize City on a motorcycle when a black vehicle entered his lane and collided with him between miles six and seven of the highway. Cus suffered severe head and abdominal injuries and later died.

Investigators later detained Rosado at his Ladyville residence, where police located a damaged 2009 Honda Ridgeline believed to have been involved in the collision. A post-mortem found that Cus died from multiple blunt-force traumatic injuries sustained in the crash.

Rosado was initially charged with five offences, including manslaughter by negligence, causing death by careless conduct, driving without due care and attention, failure to stop and render aid, and failure to report an accident. The matter ultimately proceeded in the High Court on the causing-death-by-careless-conduct charge, to which he pleaded guilty.

He is now scheduled to return before Justice Sylvester on Monday for sentencing.

World.title: Gian Teck pleads guilty to sex with 14-year-old girl after Crown Counsel Kirk Brown presents damning evidence
World.content:
Gian Teck pleads guilty to sex with 14-year-old girl after Crown Counsel Kirk Brown presents damning evidence

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Just 16 days after celebrating his 22nd birthday, Gian Teck of Maskall Village was remanded to the Belize Central Prison on Thursday after changing his plea to guilty in a High Court trial for Unlawful Sexual Intercourse (USI) with a 14-year-old minor. Teck, who stood trial before Justice Nigel Pilgrim in a judge-alone matter without a jury, conceded to defeat on the fourth day of proceedings after Crown Counsel Kirk Brown, prosecuting on behalf of the Director of Public Prosecutions (DPP), presented damning evidence and the testimony of the victim.

The trial, which commenced on Monday, September 28, 2026, hinged on the testimony of the virtual complainant, which was delivered in camera behind closed doors. According to agreed facts presented in court, the incident occurred on the night of Monday, June 5, 2023, when the 14-year-old victim visited Teck—who was 18 at the time—at his home.

The minor arrived on her bicycle, and the two went inside where Teck undressed her and engaged in sexual intercourse before she left around 1:00 a.m. the following morning. A medical examination conducted on June 29, 2023, by a doctor confirmed hymeneal tears classified as grievous harm, and during a caution interview that same day, Teck admitted to police that he had sexual intercourse with the minor three times at his residence, leading to his formal arrest on June 30, 2023.

This conviction comes months after Teck managed to avoid prosecution on separate sexual assault charges. On January 28, 2026, two counts of unlawful sexual intercourse against Teck were discontinued in the High Court before Justice Candace Nanton when the Crown entered a nolle prosequi after a victim from a May 2024 incident refused to testify, though Justice Nanton cautioned Teck at the time that the matter could be recalled in the future.

Following his guilty plea on Thursday, Justice Pilgrim revoked Teck’s bail and remanded him to the Belize Central Prison. Teck, who was represented in court by attorney Javier Williams, is scheduled to return to court on October 22, 2026, where Justice Pilgrim will hear mitigation pleas before handing down his sentence.

World.title: Kareem Anderson, charged for punching down 2 women, set free after nine months on remand without psychiatric evaluation; mother died while he was in prison
World.content:
Kareem Anderson, charged for punching down 2 women, set free after nine months on remand without psychiatric evaluation; mother died while he was in prison

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A 27-year-old Belize City man who spent approximately nine months on remand without receiving a court-ordered psychiatric evaluation has been ordered released from the Belize Central Prison after the Chief Magistrate dismissed the charges against him.

Kareem Anderson had been charged with common assault and harm in connection with separate attacks on two women in Belize City in late 2025, but the court had never taken a plea from him because of concerns about his mental state.

The Chief Magistrate noted on Wednesday that Anderson had remained behind bars for months while still awaiting an evaluation and that there was no clear indication when one could be completed.

His family reportedly could not afford a private psychiatric assessment, which can cost thousands of dollars, and the court was told that the absence of an available government psychiatrist had further delayed the process.

Given the length of time Anderson had spent on remand and the uncertainty surrounding the evaluation, the Chief Magistrate dismissed the charges and ordered that he be released as soon as possible.

Anderson had been accused of attacking two women in separate incidents captured on surveillance footage. One victim, sanitation worker Kendra Hamilton, was reportedly struck while cleaning a Belize City street, while 69-year-old Barbara Austin was allegedly punched as she walked along a sidewalk and fell to the ground.

The case also took a tragic turn while Anderson was incarcerated.

His mother, Jacqueline Elizabeth August, 54, died on August 8, 2026, while he was still on remand. Anderson’s sister, Monique, said he has not yet been told of their mother’s death and did not attend her funeral.

She said the family now faces the difficult task of breaking the news to him after his release.

Monique, who has reportedly helped care for Anderson for several years, said she expects to collect her brother from prison by Friday.

The dismissal means the allegations against Anderson will not proceed to trial at this time.

World.title: Raymond Moody granted $800 bail to seek psychiatric evaluation but remains behind bars after failing to post bail
World.content:
Raymond Moody granted $800 bail to seek psychiatric evaluation but remains behind bars after failing to post bail

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A Belize City man whose theft arraignment was previously halted because of concerns over his mental state has been granted bail so he can seek a psychiatric evaluation, but remains at the Belize Central Prison after being unable to post the required bail.

Raymond Moody, 33, appeared in the Belize City Magistrate’s Court on Wednesday, where he was offered bail in the sum of $800 with one surety of the same amount.

Moody has been in custody since late August, when his arraignment on a theft charge had to be stopped after he reportedly appeared disoriented and gave the court several different names while showing uncertainty about basic personal details including his age, date of birth and address.

At that time, Senior Magistrate Mannon Dennison ordered that Moody undergo a psychiatric evaluation before the court proceeds with the matter.

More than a month later, however, the evaluation has reportedly still not been completed.

The court has now granted Moody bail in the hope that relatives can assist him in obtaining a private psychiatric assessment so it can be determined whether he is fit to enter a plea.

Moody was unable to secure the $800 bail and was therefore remanded back to the Belize Central Prison.

The theft charge has not yet been formally put to him.

Police allege that on August 26, 2026, Moody stole a dark blue Samsung cellphone valued at $650, property of Tarique Campbell.

He is expected to return to court in December.

World.title: Family demands answers after child knocked down outside school in designated safe zone
World.content:
Family demands answers after child knocked down outside school in designated safe zone

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Santa Elena resident Britney Guerra and her family is seeking answers after her 5-year-old niece was reportedly knocked down this week by a motorcycle in front of Santa Elena Primary School in Santa Elena.

“The person operating the motorcycle is a 15-year-old boy.

When we spoke with the police, we were told that the child cannot be arrested because of his age and that he is supposed to be charged. However, as of now, we understand that he has still not been charged, and we are very concerned because the same child is still riding a motorcycle and was seen delivering food at Santa Elena Primary School on September 30th,” Guerra explained.

“We are not trying to harass or attack a 15-year-old child. We simply want answers, accountability, and reassurance that our children are safe around the school,” she added.

The family is reportedly seeking the police assistance in dealing with this matter.

World.title: Ladyville man admits attacking brother with pint bottle; court seeks help for drinking problem before sentencing
World.content:
Ladyville man admits attacking brother with pint bottle; court seeks help for drinking problem before sentencing

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A 24-year-old Ladyville man who admitted attacking his own brother with a pint bottle while drunk is out on bail pending sentencing, as the Chief Magistrate has ordered intervention from the Community Rehabilitation Department after he acknowledged having a drinking problem.

Bryan Salvatierra, a gas vendor from Ladyville, pleaded guilty to aggravated assault upon his brother, Henry Salvatierra.

According to the court facts, Henry reported that on September 28 he was lying on a sofa at home when Bryan allegedly approached him aggressively, insulted him and threatened to stab him.

Their mother reportedly intervened and separated the brothers, after which Henry called 911. Before police arrived, Bryan allegedly returned with a bottle and again threatened his brother.

When the Chief Magistrate asked Bryan what had caused the confrontation, he reportedly replied, “nothing,” before acknowledging that he had been drinking.

The court was also told that the incident was not the first time Bryan had behaved aggressively while intoxicated.

Because aggravated assault carries the possibility of a substantial prison term, the Chief Magistrate ordered a pre-sentencing report through the Community Rehabilitation Department before determining his punishment.

A social worker is expected to interview Bryan, his brother and other relatives, including their mother, as part of the assessment. The court indicated that the report could help determine whether rehabilitation or other intervention may be appropriate before sentencing.

Salvatierra was granted bail of $3,000 with one surety in the same amount. He must report to the Ladyville Police Station every Wednesday and remain at least 100 feet away from his brother and any prosecution witnesses.

He is scheduled to return to court on October 26, 2026.

World.title: JTA president-elect rushed to hospital following two- vehicle crash in Trelawny
World.content:
Scenes from a two-vehicle crash in Duncans, Trelawny, on Thursday afternoon that left President-elect of the Jamaica Teachers’ Association (JTA), Dr Maureen Mullings-Nelson, injured.

TRELAWNY, Jamaica — President-elect of the Jamaica Teachers’ Association (JTA), Dr Maureen Mullings-Nelson, was rushed to hospital on Thursday afternoon after sustaining multiple injuries in a two-vehicle crash on the Duncans main road in Trelawny.

The crash, which occurred about 3:30 pm, involved two Honda CR-V motor vehicles.

Mullings-Nelson was a passenger in one of the vehicles, which was travelling from Montego Bay, St James, towards Kingston after a JTA Central Executive meeting at the Sea Gardens Hotel.

The Jamaica Observer understands that Mullings-Nelson sustained multiple injuries and was taken to hospital for treatment.

The driver of the other Honda CR-V reportedly suffered minor injuries. It was not immediately clear whether the driver of the vehicle in which Mullings-Nelson was travelling was physically harmed.

The crash resulted in a lengthy traffic pile-up along the roadway as emergency personnel responded to the scene.

Members of the Jamaica Fire Brigade and the Jamaica Constabulary Force were among those who responded.

Further information on Mullings-Nelson’s condition were not immediately available.

World.title: ‘A me kill Taneka’: Detective testifies Ruddock confessed to Pathways killing
World.content:
Taneka Gardener was allegedly murdered on the orders of Kevin Smith at Kingdom Restoration Ministries in Albion St James.

A detective constable a few moments ago testified that murder accused Andre Ruddock confessed to him that he killed 39-year-old Taneka Gardner at the Pathways International Kingdom Restoration Ministries in Albion St James.

Gardner was killed on October 17, 2021, as part of what has been described as a human sacrifice ritual at the church.

Ruddock is alleged to have cut her throat on the instructions of his now-deceased pastor, Dr Kevin Smith, who allegedly told Gardner that her blood was unclean and therefore she had to die. The pastor allegedly asked her if she believed he could bring her back to life if she was killed. After she repeatedly said she believed, her throat was cut, allegedly by Ruddock after another man hesitated to carry out the pastor’s order to slash her throat.

Both Ruddock and Gardner were members of Smith’s flock.

The detective constable took the witness stand for the first time in the Home Circuit Court murder trial of Ruddock in downtown Kingston. He is the seventh witness to take the stand.

The detective explained that when he arrived at the scene around 11:00 pm he was pointed to two men in handcuffs who were sitting on the ground by a big gate leading to the church. One of the men was identified to the detective as Kevin Smith. The other man was identified to him as Andre Ruddock. The only sort of clothing both had on was underwear.

After receiving certain details regarding the incident, the cop led Ruddock away from the pastor and took him inside the building, where he allowed him to put on some clothes. He proceeded to caution him by telling him that he was not obliged to say anything unless he wished to do so, but that anything he said would be taken down in writing and could be used against him in a court of law.

According to him, Ruddock decided that he had something he wished to say and allegedly began to spill the beans.

“I took him away from where he was by the gate. I allowed him to put on some clothes because he was in underpants…He immediately started talking, saying, ‘a me kill Taneka, mi naa go tell you no lie and mi ago tell you everything weh happen’.

“I asked him how he killed Taneka, and he said, ‘mi cut har neck’. I asked him why he cut Taneka’s neck, and he said, ‘mi get instructions fi do it. I asked him who instructed him, and he didn’t respond, but he was looking in the direction of the big gate where I took him from,” the detective said.

The prosecution team, comprising Latoya Bernard and Carolyn Wright, will continue the examination-in-chief of the witness. In the meantime, Ruddock’s attorneys Anthony Williams and Venice Brown are listening attentively as they prepare to cross-examine the detective constable.

World.title: Water crisis deepening
World.content:
JAMAICA’S water crisis is deepening, with 107 of the National Water Commission’s 405 reserve systems dipping into drought territory, even as several parishes continue to face strict water restrictions. In the meantime, Minister of Water, Environment and Climate Change Matthew Samuda has put Jamaicans on warning for even tighter water restrictions come Monday, as the country continues to grapple with worsening drought conditions.

Some communities could be getting day-on, day-off supply as the crisis deepens, with rainfall projections for drought-affected parishes looking bleak for the months ahead.

World.title: Defence raises questions about cop who was member of Kevin Smith’s flock
World.content:
Late pastor of Pathways International Restoration Ministries, Kevin Smith.

THE detective sergeant who cried repeatedly on Tuesday while giving evidence in the Andre Ruddock murder trial in the Home Circuit Court in Kingston breathed a sigh of relief on Wednesday as she was released as a witness after defence attorney Anthony Williams ended his cross-examination of her.

Ruddock is on trial for murder in relation to the October 17, 2021 throat cutting of 39-year-old Taneka Gardner at the Pathways International Restoration Ministries in Albion, St James.

On Wednesday, the witness was more composed on the stand as Williams quizzed her on the happenings at the church where Gardner and two male members were killed. One of the men was killed allegedly by the late pastor of the church, Dr Kevin Smith. The other man was shot and killed by the police after he attacked lawmen with a knife.

The detective sergeant was the initial investigator assigned to the case before it was turned over to a more senior cop.

On the day of the incident, the pastor was said to have taken a Glock pistol from a female member of the Jamaica Constabulary Force (JCF) who was also a member of the church. The pastor used that firearm to shoot at the police.

When the incident was brought to an end, the police carted away numerous individuals, including Smith and the members of his church, to a police station where criminal charges were laid against them.

The female cop, who had a close relationship with Smith, was among those who were arrested. She was charged for breaching the Disaster Risk Management Act (DRMA) during COVID-19 lockdowns when no one, except for essential workers, was supposed to be on the road. Under the Act, large gatherings were prohibited.

Williams, who is one of two attorneys representing Ruddock, along with Venice Brown, asked the witness whether any other charges were laid against the female police member of Smith’s flock.

The attorney enquired if the cop was ever referred to the Inspectorate and Professional Standards Oversight Bureau (IPROB), which is a disciplinary unit within the JCF.

“Is this arm of the JCF responsible for complaints and investigations into the conduct of any member of the JCF?” Williams asked.

The witness told him that to the best of her knowledge that was, in fact, so.

The attorney wanted to know why the cop wasn’t referred to IPROB, but no definitive answer was given to that question.

The witness told the court that when the female constable was arrested, she was taken to an area of the church which looked like living quarters where she handed over a bag that contained her private Glock pistol, handcuffs, a video recorder, personal items, as well as her police uniform.

“As indicated to me, it was a private firearm,” the witness said.

Williams asked her if the constable’s hands were swabbed, and the witness said she personally did not swab her hands but gave instructions for that activity to be carried out; however, she could not speak to the outcome of the swabbing.

“When you first saw her on the 17th of October 2021, did she say anything to you?” Williams asked.

The witness responded in the affirmative, saying that she did speak to the cop, and that she said several things.

The lawyer sought to find out if whatever was said was indicative of her involvement at Pathways International Kingdom Restoration Ministries.

“In light of the several utterances, did it lead you to carry out any further investigation?” the attorney asked.

“Yes, sir, certainly,” the witness said, before explaining that she was not the person who charged the constable.

She explained further that she did not know who exactly charged the constable for breaching the DRMA.

The trial continues today with a new witness. The seven members of the jury are expected to view photographs of the scene at the church as described by the six witnesses who have taken the stand so far during the trial which started two weeks ago.

World.title: Kabaka Pyramid still has lots to say
World.content:
Kabaka Pyramid.

There is still a rebel in Kabaka Pyramid. Fifteen years after the Rebel Music era first introduced audiences to that particular side of his artistry, the Kingston-born musician has chosen to revisit familiar territory — but he is not quite the same man who entered it.

Though the lyrical sharpness and the instinct to make music that says something beyond simply sounding good remains, time and a few battles of his own have added new layers to the story.

That evolution is recognisable in his latest single A Warrior’s Pain, a collaboration with American rappers R-Mean and Styles P.

The track serves as the foundation for Rebel Music 1 & 2, a new lyrics tape marking 15 years since the beginning of the entertainer’s Rebel Music chapter.

For Kabaka Pyramid, the return was not the result of an elaborate master plan. In fact, it was almost accidental.

“We knew the 15-year anniversary of Rebel Music was approaching and also the 10-year anniversary of the Accurate mixtape,” he explained. “So my team and I were floating around ideas since the start of the year. We were keeping it simple — samples and hip hop drums,” he said. “I just wanted something that inspired me to be lyrical.”

That instinct reignited something the artiste said had perhaps become dormant.

“It felt like I had suppressed a part of my craft and it needed to be reawakened,” he said outlining that the first few tracks were a hit with his manager, who remarked that they sounded like the

Rebel Music days.

“That moment was when we knew what had to be done,” he said. “Everything flowed easily from there.”

That renewed focus on lyricism sits alongside another important thread in Kabaka Pyramid’s current work — vulnerability.

On A Warrior’s Pain, the entertainer brings together reggae and hip hop through a shared appreciation for substance, storytelling, and resistance. But beneath the lyrical exchanges and musical chemistry, A Warrior’s Pain speaks to a more personal kind of battle

Kabaka Pyramid points to his own struggle with confidence in his voice and singing ability as part of the experience informing his contribution.

“I was always being told I need more melody, songs need to be more catchy, simplify the music,” he said. But, rather than resist the criticism, he used it as motivation.

“So I put in the hours to train myself and be ready for anything when called upon,” he explained. “Overcoming challenges is the best way to build confidence and strength comes from there naturally.”

That growth is perhaps one of the clearest differences between the Kabaka Pyramid of the early days and the artiste he has become.

“The message is still the same, just more mature now,” he said. “I think more people can relate to what I’m saying. It’s not music only for hip hop heads that love to dissect lyrical patterns.”

With that said, Kabaka Pyramid shared that the response to reggae and conscious music from international audiences continues to surprise him, particularly in Africa, Europe, Japan, and the United States. This is sees as not cultural appropriation, but an opportunity to observe how others interpret and conduct business around Jamaican music.

“When others incorporate our music I like to learn from them, and see what aspects they connect with and also how they conduct the business of touring,” he said.

There is, however, one boundary: “If you sample my record I want what is rightfully mine,” he said with a laugh.

World.title: Green calls for regional farmworker framework
World.content:
Belize’s Minister of Agriculture, Food Security and Enterprise, Rodwell Ferguson (left) speaking on Wednesday during a plenary session on “Unlocking private sector partnerships and expanding investments in agriculture and fisheries development” during the Caribbean Week of Agriculture 2026 conference at Ocean Coral Spring Hotel in Trelawny. Looking on is Floyd Green, Jamaica’s agriculture minister. (Photo: Horace Hines)

CORAL SPRING, Trelawny — Agriculture Minister Floyd Green is calling for a regional structure to facilitate the movement of agricultural workers across the Caribbean, pointing to Dominica as a model for easing constraints on farmers and boosting production.

“I think we need a framework, a framework that works for the movement of agricultural workers across the region,” he said.

He noted that Dominica has already established a framework for agricultural migrant workers which has enabled the country to bring in about 200 workers, benefiting roughly 80 farmers and contributing to a significant increase in productivity.

Green was speaking during Wednesday’s plenary session on “Unlocking private sector partnerships and expanding investments in agriculture and fisheries development” at the Caribbean Week of Agriculture 2026 conference. It was held at Ocean Coral Spring Hotel in Trelawny.

The session, on the fourth of the six-day conference, followed a question from the floor about region-wide difficulty finding workers for agriculture.

Green said the Caribbean should reconsider its traditionally insular approach to agricultural labour.

“If given the opportunity, just as they are given the opportunity to go to Canada and to go to America and they work and they return home…what about the region?” he asked.

He said a regional mechanism could allow workers to take up agricultural employment in neighbouring territories while providing farmers with access to people willing to work within the sector.

Green acknowledged that such an arrangement would require proper oversight, but said Dominica’s experience provides a model worth examining. He said he intends to raise the matter at the Caribbean Community’s Council for Trade and Economic Development (COTED).

At the same time, Green said the region must make greater use of technology as the profile of the agricultural workforce changes.

“One of the challenges with the young people going into agriculture now, they want to be owners. They don’t want to be workers,” he said, stressing the need to provide them with tools that can improve efficiency and productivity.

Green cited agricultural drones as one example of how technology can reduce reliance on manual tasks.

Through the Rural Agricultural Development Authority (RADA), Jamaica has invested in four drones which farmers may rent. They come with trained drone pilots. The College of Agriculture, Science and Education (CASE) is also training drone operators, while Jamaican company Sky Crop has begun assembling agricultural drones locally.

Green also pointed to the growing use of small walk-behind tractors, which can enable individual farmers to more efficiently manage their operations.

He said artificial intelligence (AI) and other emerging technologies should form part of the region’s response as agriculture adapts to changing workforce patterns.

Belize’s Minister of Agriculture, Food Security and Enterprise Rodwell Ferguson said his country has experienced a similar shift.

He recalled that three to four decades ago, Belize relied on agricultural workers from neighbouring Guatemala, Honduras, and El Salvador. That has changed as more young Belizeans have gained access to secondary and tertiary education, including university and postgraduate studies.

“Young people are getting the opportunity to go to high school, sixth form, universities, [do] master’s degree, doctorate degree. And so maybe it is a good reason for the advent of the AI because it’s a time when we are having labour shortage, and no matter what we do, we can’t convince those young people to go and do agriculture,” he said.

Ferguson said the changing aspirations of young people are also reflected in schools.

In Belize, he said, agriculture is compulsory in first and second form but becomes an elective in third and fourth form. By then, participation can fall to about five students.

Ferguson said smart agriculture could help make the sector more attractive to young people while helping Belize meet its food production needs.

“It is critical. It is crucial because we must be able to feed ourselves,” he said.

World.title: UNITED BEHIND INFANTINO
World.content:
FIFA President Gianni Infantino (left) speaks with British Virgin Islands Football Association President Avanell Morton during the launch of the island’s new technical centre on Saturday. (Photo: FIFA Media)

The Jamaica Football Federation (JFF) will not be alone in backing FIFA President Gianni Infantino with fellow Caribbean associations of Trinidad and Tobago, British Virgin Islands, Antigua and Barbuda, and St Kitts and Nevis also on board.

Infantino recently completed his tour of the Caribbean at the weekend with many critics believing the trip was used to try to secure votes as he seeks to remain FIFA president for another four years ahead of the body’s congress in Morocco in March.

Infantino, 54, has led FIFA since 2016 and has faced increased scrutiny over the past few months after his controversial plan to sell stakes in FIFA competitions, including the men’s and women’s World Cup, to private investors. This plan was eventually scrapped last month after widespread backlash. Infantino’s recent Caribbean visit was his second in a matter of weeks after attending the Caribbean Football Union Presidents’ Meeting in the Dominican Republic. He was advised prior by his FIFA vice-president and Concacaf President Victor Montagliani to stay away from the event.

His first stop was in Kingston on Friday where he met with JFF officials, including President Michael Ricketts, and attended the Reggae Boyz’s 3-2 win over Guatemala in the Concacaf Nations League at the National Stadium.

As the Jamaica Observer reported on Sunday, the JFF will back Infantino in the upcoming elections with the board of directors in favour of him staying.

Ricketts told the Observer in August that he would support Infantino, given what he describes as massive support he’s given to football, particularly in the Caribbean.

Ricketts reiterated his support for Infantino after his one-day visit to the island.

“I think Infantino has done so very well for football globally,” he said. “I remember when I got into football as the president, the support from FIFA was medial to say the least.It has been a lot better now and we are just very grateful and we are looking forward to further improvements so that we can impact not just football but the social well-being of every boy and girl who plays the sport.”

Also in Kingston during Infantino’s visit was Trinidad and Tobago Football Association (TFFA) Kieron Edwards who also attended the game on Friday. Trinidad’s senior men’s team played Haiti at Sabina Park a day before.

In 2020, FIFA appointed a normalisation committee to manage the TTFA’s affairs due to serious financial issues. However, it was lifted in 2024 with Edwards being named president.

Edwards says FIFA has helped to reshape football in his country.

“FIFA is our largest supporter when it comes to our infrastructure,” he said. “Even our leagues, when we look at our women’s league now, [it’s a] full professional league, playing for seven months for the year, over 12 teams. That was only [possible because of] the continued support of FIFA in terms of our games. When it comes to the support of FIFA in terms of growing football, not just in Trinidad and Tobago but across the Caribbean and Concacaf, it’s been tremendous so far.”

Edwards says he has no doubts that the TTFA will be backing Infantino at the elections next year.

“We would have given President Infantino our full support and we have not wavered with that. Things do come up, changes, you have to have discussions, you have to have dialogue but the support is there 100 per cent behind the President always.”

British Virgin Islands (BVI) Football Association president Avanell Morton has also thrown his support behind Infantino.

Infantino visited BVI on Saturday and opened the new BVI Technical Centre, which was funded by FIFA.

“What more can he do? He’s doing a fantastic job already. He’s doing a fantastic job in the entire region,” Morton said.

The Antigua and Barbuda Football Association (ABFA), led by President Ickford Roberts, is also in favour of Infantino staying on as president. Infantino visited the island on Saturday and met with Roberts and Prime Minister Gaston Browne, who announced that a new football stadium would be built with FIFA support.

“[Infantino’s] transformative policies, from ground-breaking investment in grassroots infrastructure to the historic expansion of World Cup access, have elevated the aspirations of emerging football nations into attainable realities,” the ABFA said in a statement recently. “By listening with genuine humility and acting with decisive conviction, he has forged a legacy of inclusivity that transcends the sport itself, affirming that every nation, regardless of size, deserves equal voice and fair opportunity on the world stage.”

Infantino also visited St Kitts and Nevis on Saturday, where he attended the launch of a new technical centre with St Kitts and Nevis Football Association President Atiba Hattis president giving his support.

Infantino could have as many as 25 Caribbean votes behind him if all of the region’s FIFA member associations support his bid.

No one has signalled intentions to challenge Infantino with nominations closing on November 18, but it’s understood that Montagliani is seen as a credible opponent who would receive the backing of Europe (UEFA) and the Asian Football Confederation.

World.title: Dinner @ OMNIA SKY LOUNGE
World.content:
(Photo: Aceion Cunningham)

Nestled atop Parkway Plaza in Ocho Rios, Omnia Sky Lounge has quickly become more than just a dining spot — it’s the embodiment of Jamaican flavour, international influences, and vibrant nightlife. Since its grand opening in April 2024, this rooftop haven has been captivating locals and tourists alike with its unique blend of great food, lively music, and inviting ambience.

For owner Doneisha Johnson, the journey to creating Omnia Sky Lounge is rooted in her travels, taking cues from stunning rooftop lounges in Indonesia and Los Angeles. Her previous venture, a Loud Fashion store in Ocho Rios, serendipitously provided the perfect platform — the rooftop space above the store — to birth a new concept. She envisioned a place that brought together food, music, ambience, and entertainment in a seamless, memorable offering.

“It was about creating something different. A place where people don’t just come to eat, but to immerse themselves in an unforgettable experience,” Johnson said.

Omnia Sky Lounge embraces the tagline ‘Dinner With a Vibe,’ aiming to transcend the typical dining experience. Whether guests come for a celebratory occasion, a casual night out, or an exclusive event, the lounge promises an atmosphere that lingers in memory long after the night ends.

The concept is clear and intentional — a fusion where the essence of Caribbean cuisine meets international flair, showcased in a setting alive with music, thoughtfully crafted cocktails, and a welcoming environment.

The menu showcases contemporary Caribbean dishes infused with Jamaican flavours — seafood, chicken, pork, curry goat, and pastas — all prepared with Omnia’s distinctive twist. Alongside enticing bites is an impressive beverage selection featuring signature cocktails, premium spirits, wines, Champagne, and bottle service.

Feedback has been overwhelmingly positive, cementing Omnia as a destination for locals and visitors, with the lounge becoming a favoured spot for special occasions like birthdays, weddings, corporate events, and family reunions.

“Seeing customers return and recommending us has been extremely rewarding. Sometimes I stand back and remember when Omnia was simply an idea in my head. Seeing people choose us for something as important as their wedding makes the challenges of entrepreneurship feel worthwhile,” Johnson expressed.

Johnson has ambitious plans for Omnia’s growth, aiming to enhance the existing space with an additional level and dedicated event areas. An exciting new concept centred on regulated cannabis is also under consideration, pending licensing and approvals.

“Our plans include adding another upper level above the kitchen area and two dedicated event spaces at the rear of the property. The goal is to continue developing Omnia into a complete dining, entertainment, events, and lifestyle destination. Long term, I definitely see the Omnia brand expanding beyond Ocho Rios,” Johnson added.

Johnson also expressed gratitude to her loyal customers, dedicated staff and excitement for the future.

“We’re proud of what we’ve built, excited about what’s ahead, and still building. My vision is for Omnia Sky Lounge to become a must-visit destination when people come to Ocho Rios and Jamaica,” Johnson concluded.

Text & Photos: Aceion Cunningham

World.title: Conservative ex-mayor Andy Street out of the running for top railways job
World.content:
Both of the people said a key reason was that Street still appeared to harbor a desire to return to frontline politics. One of the people, a government official, said he had been “unable to subdue his political ambitions.” Street was the Conservative mayor of the West Midlands for seven years until Labour narrowly defeated him in 2024.

Street declined to comment on the Great British Railways recruitment process, and told POLITICO that supposition about his political intentions was “speculation” and “conjecture.”

‘Political ambitions’

Recruitment began in January for the role of chair, which will pay £200,000 to £300,000 a year for 10 days of work a month. Great British Railways is due to be up and running in 2027, with passenger services transferred to public ownership by the end of that year as private rail operators’ contracts expire.

The Department for Transport declined to comment on whether a decision was imminent or the process of finding a chair had slowed. A government official said a “fair, open and merit-based process” was underway.

Street has history with Britain’s railways. He narrowly decided not to quit the Conservatives in 2023 when former Prime Minister Rishi Sunak scrapped a leg of the planned High Speed 2 rail line from Birmingham to Manchester.

Supporters describe him as a figure who reached across political lines and was respected for his nine-year stint as managing director of department store John Lewis.

World.title: Burnham wants to change British elections. Voters think they’re fine as is.
World.content:
At the same time, the survey revealed potential openness to a system of proportional representation, in which the number of parliamentary seats each party wins is more closely linked to the total number of votes it receives across the country.

“Most people don’t spend much time thinking about how we elect MPs and, broadly, people think the current system is fair,” said Seb Wride, head of polling at Public First. “Burnham will need to make a convincing case to voters about why changing the electoral system is necessary, if he is to gain support for his plans.”

Under first-past-the-post, whichever candidate wins the most votes in their constituency is elected to represent that seat, even if they fall far short of a majority of local voters. Nationally, that can result in a party taking power with relatively low popular support.

Labour won the last election in 2024 by a landslide, taking 63% of seats in Parliament with just 34% of the vote — the most disproportionate result in British history.

Since then, some polling projections have suggested Nigel Farage’s populist-right Reform UK party was on track to win a majority with around 30% of votes under the first-past-the-post system.

In a speech to Labour members in Liverpool, Burnham said recent turbulence in British politics — he’s the country’s seventh prime minister in 10 years — meant a new system was needed. “We will all have failed in our public duties if we carry on as we are and open the door of No. 10 to a divisive government on less than 30% of the vote,” he said.

World.title: Europe war-games life after Merz
World.content:
It’s not a prospect they take lightly. Merz leads the EU’s largest economy and is the chief negotiator for wealthy countries seeking to rein in spending in the bloc’s proposed €2 trillion seven-year budget. He is also a driving force behind EU efforts to save heavy industry.

“Any debate about the German chancellor weakens Germany’s role in the EU and in the world,” said Wilhelm Gebhard, a member of the Bundestag and an official in Merz’s governing CDU party.

With France facing its own far-right surge and a presidential election next year that could hand power to euroskeptic Marine Le Pen, few in Brussels relish the prospect of Germany, historically the EU’s other major player, turning inwards or derailing important negotiations.

The contingency planning, which has seen officials and diplomats brainstorm the situation, comes after months of mixed signals from Berlin on EU policy, including car emissions and a proposed social media ban for children. Even if Merz stays in office, the political turmoil is already complicating Berlin’s work on the EU’s biggest files.

The worst-case scenario for Brussels would be a leaderless Germany, or one with a far-right government. But that is seen as virtually impossible in the short term, with none of the mainstream players seeking new elections while the far-right Alternative for Germany party are leading in the polls.

“All coalition partners know that they have a great deal to lose from early elections,” said Hannah Neumann, an opposition Green MEP who sits on the European Parliament’s security and foreign affairs committees. “My expectation, therefore, is that they will stay together and muddle through.”

World.title: It’s the end of the world as we know it (and I feel an investment opportunity coming on)
World.content:
That means humankind will outlast the EU, as the bloc’s demise is penciled in for May 2027, when either French far-right leader Marine Le Pen or far-left leader Jean-Luc Mélenchon will march into Brussels with a flaming pitchfork (unless they do it on a Friday, in which case no one will be there to see it).

Between now and the end of the world, AI will replace all jobs except those that absolutely, categorically cannot be done by a machine because they are essential and require a delicate human touch: nurse, electrician, writer of weekly satirical columns …

But what if you’ve got loads of money you want to invest and yet you have some concerns about the impending apocalypse? That was the conundrum posed this week as Anthropic prepared for a potential $2 trillion flotation (as in when a company offers shares to the public — not when you’re on holiday in a pool, lying on a piece of plastic shaped like a donut).

Anthropic issued a prospectus outlining its finances, growth plans and risk profile to potential investors that warns AI models could exhibit “self-preserving behaviours”, including attempts to “resist shutdown,” to “conceal or manipulate information” and behavior “resembling blackmail.”

So on the one hand, AI could refuse to shut down and try and blackmail us, but on the other hand, there’s a chance to make some cash by investing in a growth industry. What’s an investor to do?

Despite all the doom and gloom, though, there’s still hope for humanity. This week, the White House signed an accord on “Super Intelligence” — that’s just AI — signed by the likes of xAI CEO Elon Musk, Google CEO Sundar Pichai and Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, as well as noted intelligence fan U.S. President Donald Trump. Alas, the latter was described in the accord as “President of the Unites States” with an “s” instead of the “d.”

World.title: ‘Tough’ talks with China have yet to deliver, EU trade chief says
World.content:
Šefčovič travels to Beijing Oct. 8 for what he termed a “a super crucial meeting” with Chinese Commerce Minister Wang Wentao, and said he was optimistic the trip will bear fruit. “You have to believe that you can accomplish something, otherwise you better don’t go.”

The commissioner needs to get results he can present at a meeting of EU leaders in Brussels on Oct. 15-16, and has said previously that Brussels is ready to restrict Chinese access to the EU market should the talks fail.

The EU and China have been locked in tense negotiations since June. EU leaders have said they can no longer tolerate the flood of Chinese imports inundating the single market, putting pressure on domestic manufacturers and forcing plant closures and layoffs.

“I think our Chinese partners understood that this has direct implication on the future of emblematic European companies — literally thousands of jobs,” Šefčovič reported. “And also the social fabric and social model which was developed in Europe over many, many decades.”

The bloc’s ballooning €1-billion-a-day trade deficit with China lies at the heart of the talks. Cutting that deficit would require either reducing imports from China, boosting EU exports, or a mix of the two.

Šefčovič said he hopes to bring a “proof of concept” back from Beijing that addresses three main issues: sudden Chinese export surges in key industrial sectors; tangible ways to increase European goods exports to China; and long-term clarity regarding China’s export curbs on raw materials, especially rare earth elements.

World.title: Albania’s PM to US Democrats: Don’t use us to get revenge on Trump
World.content:
He added: “I told my Democratic friends in America: If you cannot beat Trump in America, do not come to Albania to take revenge. That is not fair.”

Kushner is linked to a multi-billion-dollar project to develop a luxury resort on the uninhabited southern Albanian island of Sazan and an adjacent strip of shoreline next to a protected area inhabited by flamingos, pelicans and diverse wetland wildlife. The plans sparked national and international protests at the end of May, with rallies ongoing every night outside Rama’s office in Tirana.

The protests drew widespread attention, with a resolution in the European Parliament, and international clothing brand Patagonia, and Kosovo-Albanian pop singer Dua Lipa getting involved.

Rama said the plans involve two projects: One on the publicly owned Sazan Island, a former Soviet military base, with only 8% to be developed, and another on a privately owned peninsula.

Protestors object to the project over environmental concerns and a lack of public consultation. Meanwhile, the country’s EU- and U.S.-backed Special Prosecutor’s Office for Organized Crime and Corruption, SPAK, is investigating whether an Albanian businessman faked ownership documents related to the private land.

The former owner has denied any wrongdoing. A spokesperson for the project’s investors, including Kushner, did not respond to a request for comment by the time of publication.

World.title: As Germany’s far right rises, weakened Merz looks to project strength and resolve against Putin
World.content:
Merz went on to warn of the danger of conflict in Europe with some of his most dramatic language yet.

“Would the Baltic states then become a battlefield for drone warfare, just as Donbas is today?” he said. “Which major European cities would be targeted by the ballistic missiles that Russia is currently firing at the populations of Kyiv and Kharkiv?"

“Would we Germans ultimately be targeted as well? Would we once again experience the horrors of war firsthand? Ladies and gentlemen, our most urgent European and transatlantic responsibility today is to do everything in our power to avert this.”

Merz’s comments came weeks after the far-right Alternative for Germany party recorded its best-ever election results, coming in first in two regional votes in the former East Germany, while the chancellor’s conservative Christian Democratic Union suffered historic defeats. The conservatives’ poor results were widely blamed on the deeply unpopular chancellor, prompting internal debate within his own party over whether to replace him.

The surge in popularity for the Kremlin-friendly AfD sparked concerns in Kyiv and across Europe that Germany — which under Merz has become Ukraine’s greatest military supporter — could falter in its support for Ukraine. The AfD — a party that favors ending military support for Ukraine and re-establishing economic and energy ties with Moscow — is the most popular party in the country, according to surveys, polling well above Merz’s conservatives.

Merz on Thursday took aim at the AfD, portraying the party as a conduit for Moscow’s influence and vowing that his government would continue to support Ukraine despite hybrid attacks and disinformation campaigns “orchestrated from Moscow” and spread through “the slogans of the AfD and its Russian backers.”

World.title: Danish military admits flaws in report about 2025 drone incursions
World.content:
The Danish Armed Forces have admitted to have made errors in their initial report on suspected drones of unknown origins that flew over the country in the autumn of 2025.

 

In the run-up to a EU summit in Copenhagen at the beginning of October, drones had been sighted both above civilian and military air bases, causing heightened security measures, temporary airport shutdowns and a private drone ban.

The sites affected included Skrydstrup air base -- where Ukrainian pilots are trained on F-16 fighter jets.

Following some scepticism about the official version of events, this June the government and military confirmed that drones had flown over the country, even though their origin was still unknown.

Denmark's military also released a report about its handling of the incidents.

However their detailed account of one incident was called into question after media reported that witness accounts contradicting their version.

That prompted Defence Minister Jeppe Bruus to ask for a review.

In the revised report of the incident released Thursday, the military admitted that their account might have been mistaken.

Soldiers may have fired into the air while a civilian aircraft passed by, they said, as had been suggested by some aviation and drone experts.

But it stressed that their assessment was still that the soldiers had fired upon what was believed to have been a drone, based among other things on its flight pattern.

"The unit deployed in Borris was carrying out a sensitive guard duty whose purpose was to protect Ukrainian trainees in the camp, and the unit observed drones over the Borris camp on 24, 25, and 28 September 2025," it said.

Denmark has since worked on enhancing her anti-drone and drone-detection capacities.
